<!--
READING ORDER

This file is ordered as the analysis runs, top to bottom. Run the chunks in
order once and every figure and table in the manuscript is produced; nothing
below needs a second pass over anything above it.

  1  Export expression        writes the .mtx for the stiffness analysis
  2  Configuration            constants, helpers, plotting functions. No data,
                              no computation. Cheap; re-run whenever the code
                              changes.
  3  Data                     metadata merge, MSigDB gene sets, matrisome list
  4  Compartment + cluster tests
  5  Global pooled test
  6  Leading-edge redundancy
  7  Meta-modules across tests
  8  Over-representation analysis (optional; threshold-respecting)
  9  Curation step 1          writes the *_toplot.csv QC templates
 10  Curation step 2          MANUAL EDIT, then the curated dot plots
 11  Matrisome by category, and the ligand-receptor scatter
 12  Supplementary tables
  A  Appendix: replot from saved CSVs (only needed if a threshold changes)

  4 and 5 need 2 and 3. 5 does not need 4. 9 needs the CSVs from 4/5 (and 8 if
  ORA templates are wanted). 10 needs YOUR edits to the files 9 wrote.

  Objects defined in 2 live in the global environment for the whole session, so
  a session holding definitions from an older version of this file would
  silently use the OLD ones. Chunk 2 carries CONFIG_VERSION and every consuming
  chunk calls assert_config_current(), which stops on a mismatch.

WHAT CHANGED WHEN THIS FILE WAS TIDIED FOR SUBMISSION
  Three things were folded into the main run so that the manuscript figures
  come out of a single pass. The numbers are unchanged; only the order and the
  point at which figures are drawn moved.

  - The matrisome volcano was a separate replot chunk. plot_volcano now takes
    matri_tbl and run_deg_gsea passes it, so both the plain and the
    matrisome-outlined figure are written on the first run, under the same
    filenames as before (Volcano_*, Volcano-matrisome_*). Same colouring rule,
    same top-10-per-direction labelling, same 3.5 x 4.0 in geometry.

  - GO:CC and GO:MF were added by a second GSEA chunk that re-ran fgsea and
    overwrote the result CSVs. All five collections are now loaded in chunk 3
    and tested in one pass. This is not cosmetic: BH correction runs across the
    whole tested family, so a Hallmark set's padj depends on how many GO sets
    were tested with it. Testing all five at once is what makes the padj in the
    figures and the padj in the curated tables the same number. The old
    two-pass route left the automatic dot plots drawn from a three-collection
    run while the CSVs held five.

  - plot_gsea_dot called scale_colour_viridis_c while the mapped aesthetic was
    fill (shape 21). A colour scale applies to nothing there, so ggplot fell
    back to its default blue fill gradient and the legend carried the raw
    column name. It is now scale_fill_viridis_c with the same settings as the
    curated manuscript dot plot, so the automatic and curated figures match.

  The curation chunks (9 and 10) are unchanged and remain a manual step.
  Existing *_toplot.csv files are never overwritten unless CURATE_OVERWRITE is
  TRUE, so the curated pathway selections behind the manuscript figures are not
  affected by re-running anything here.

STATISTICS, in one paragraph
  DESeq2 is run with the ordinary Wald test, H0: log2FoldChange = 0. That is
  the two-sided default and it returns both directions: negative LFC = higher
  in Young, positive LFC = higher in Aged. LFC_THRESHOLD and PADJ_CUTOFF are
  applied AFTER the test, purely to draw the lines on the volcano, colour the
  points, count DEGs and choose labels. They are not part of the null. Change
  them and re-run only the appendix chunk; the DESeq2 fit does not change.

  GSEA does not use the threshold at all. It ranks EVERY tested gene by the
  signed Wald statistic and looks for coordinated shifts, which is why a gene
  set can be significant with no single member passing |LFC| > 1. Changing the
  threshold therefore leaves every NES and every GSEA padj unchanged. The
  optional ORA chunk is the analysis that does respect the threshold.
-->


# 1. Export log-norm expression

Exports only bins with a valid nanoindentation so the matrix stays small.
```{r export-expression}
library(Seurat)
library(Matrix)
library(DESeq2)
library(fgsea)
library(msigdbr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(tibble)
library(grid)

## Load last RDS using detected path
merge.full <- readRDS(
  "Z:/Visium_Data/01_Multi-sample-integration/merge_full_HarmonyBANKSY_SeuratClusters_annotated.rds")

# Load the SpatialX metadata TSV (output of map_centroids_to_bins.py)
metadata_tsv_path <- "Z:/Visium_Data/001_SpatialX/20260803_FinalAnnotatedMetadata/metadata_with_nano.tsv"

meta_tsv <- read.delim(metadata_tsv_path, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Keep only bins with a valid nanoindentation measurement
meta_valid <- meta_tsv[meta_tsv$valid_measurement == "True", ]
cat("Bins with valid mechanical measurements:", nrow(meta_valid), "\n")

# Reconstruct the barcode_full identifier used as colnames(merge.full):
#   barcode_full = "{Barcodes}.{sample_name}"   e.g. "s_004um_00000_00796-1.CA_01"
meta_valid$barcode_full <- paste0(meta_valid$Barcodes, ".", meta_valid$CaptureArea)

# Ensure RNA assay is joined and is the default
DefaultAssay(merge.full) <- "RNA"
merge.full[["RNA"]] <- JoinLayers(merge.full[["RNA"]])

# Subset to only the barcodes present in BOTH the metadata and the Seurat object
barcodes_keep <- intersect(meta_valid$barcode_full, colnames(merge.full))
cat("Barcodes matched to Seurat object:", length(barcodes_keep),
    "/", nrow(meta_valid), "\n")
if (length(barcodes_keep) == 0) {
  stop("No overlap between metadata barcode_full and merge.full colnames.\n",
       "Check that meta_valid$Barcodes and meta_valid$sample_name ",
       "match the structure of colnames(merge.full).")
}

obj_sub <- subset(merge.full, cells = barcodes_keep)

# Extract log-normalised expression (genes x cells)
expr <- GetAssayData(obj_sub, assay = "RNA", layer = "data")
cat("Expression matrix:", nrow(expr), "genes x", ncol(expr), "cells\n")
# Coerce to a Matrix::dgCMatrix so writeMM has a method
expr_mat <- as(expr, "dgCMatrix")

# Export as MatrixMarket format + barcode/feature lists
metadata_dir <- dirname(metadata_tsv_path)
out_dir <- file.path(metadata_dir, "expression_export")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

meta_export <- meta_valid[match(colnames(obj_sub), meta_valid$barcode_full), ]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ADDED: carry sequencing depth through to the export so script 10 can test
# the detection-depth confound (deeper bins detect more genes, which would
# inflate every gene's correlation with stiffness in the same direction).
# match() above aligns meta_export to colnames(obj_sub), so these two vectors
# are already in the same order as the columns of obj_sub.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
meta_export$nCount_RNA   <- obj_sub$nCount_RNA
meta_export$nFeature_RNA <- obj_sub$nFeature_RNA

Matrix::writeMM(expr_mat, file.path(out_dir, "step9_expression_matrix.mtx"))
writeLines(colnames(expr), file.path(out_dir, "step9_expression_barcodes.txt"))
writeLines(rownames(expr), file.path(out_dir, "step9_expression_features.txt"))
write.table(meta_export,
            file.path(out_dir, "step9_expression_metadata_matched.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

cat("Export complete:", out_dir, "\n")
#```

# 2. Configuration: constants, helpers, plotting functions

#step9_expression_barcodes.txt (barcodes / bins, one per column);
#step9_expression_features.txt (gene names, one per row);
#step9_expression_metadata_matched.tsv (metadata for the same ~96,000 bins,
#including nanoindentation measurements, nCount_RNA and nFeature_RNA).

## Config: constants, helpers, plotting functions

#```{r DEG-GSEA-config}
CONFIG_VERSION <- "2026-08-31_v1"   # bump whenever this chunk changes

METADATA_TSV <- r"(Z:\Visium_Data\001_SpatialX\20260803_FinalAnnotatedMetadata\HTO_Combined_4um_Images\metadata\HTO_Combined_4um_Images_annotated_data.tsv)"
OUTPUT_DIR   <- file.path(
  r"(Z:\Visium_Data\001_SpatialX\20260803_FinalAnnotatedMetadata)",
  "deg_gsea_outputs")

TSV_BARCODE_COL  <- "Barcodes"
TSV_SAMPLE_COL   <- "CaptureArea"
TSV_CLUSTER_COL  <- "CellCluster"
TSV_AGE_COL      <- "AgeGroup"
TSV_TISSUE_COL   <- "Tissue-slices"

# ---- post-hoc significance rules -------------------------------------------
# These are NOT part of the DESeq2 null hypothesis. DESeq2 runs the ordinary
# two-sided Wald test, H0: LFC = 0. These two values only draw the lines on the
# volcano, colour the points, count DEGs and pick labels. Both directions are
# always kept: LFC < -LFC_THRESHOLD is higher in Young, LFC > +LFC_THRESHOLD is
# higher in Aged. Changing either value requires only the replot chunk.
LFC_THRESHOLD <- 1        # dashed vertical lines at -1 and +1
PADJ_CUTOFF   <- 0.05     # dashed horizontal line at -log10(0.05) = 1.301

# Which LFC column the threshold is applied to, and which is plotted on x.
#   "log2FoldChange"      apeglm posterior estimate. DESeq2's own
#                         recommendation for visualisation and ranking.
#   "log2FoldChange_mle"  the unshrunken MLE, the quantity the Wald test
#                         actually tested. Use this if a reviewer objects to
#                         thresholding a shrunken estimate.
DEG_LFC_COL <- "log2FoldChange"

MIN_CELLS_PER_SAMPLE <- 10

GSEA_LE_JACCARD <- 0.5

GSEA_MIN_SIZE <- 10
GSEA_MAX_SIZE <- 500
GSEA_NPERM    <- 10000

# Pseudobulk gene filter. A gene is kept if it exceeds MIN_COUNT_PER_SAMPLE in
# at least MIN_SAMPLES_DETECTED pseudobulk samples. (5, 2) is permissive: with
# 8 animals a gene detected in only 2 of 8 survives, and genes near-zero in
# every Young animal but present in two Aged animals land in the far tail of
# the volcano with large |LFC| and large SE. Raising MIN_SAMPLES_DETECTED to
# min(n_young, n_aged) removes that tail. Left at the original values so
# nothing changes silently.
MIN_COUNT_PER_SAMPLE <- 5
MIN_SAMPLES_DETECTED <- 2

# Save the fitted DESeqDataSet per test. Small (a few MB) and it means any
# future change to LFC_THRESHOLD, PADJ_CUTOFF or figure style never requires
# refitting. Set FALSE to skip.
SAVE_DDS <- TRUE

# ---- figure geometry and output formats ------------------------------------
FIG_DPI     <- 600      # PNG resolution; SVG is vector so dpi is irrelevant there
VOLCANO_W   <- 3.5      # = 7 / 2
VOLCANO_H   <- 4.0      # = 6 * 2/3
GSEA_DOT_W  <- 6.5      # pathway names are long; narrower is not readable
VOLCANO_N_LABEL <- 15   # 20 labels in a 3.5 in panel collide badly

VOLCANO_PANEL_MM <- list(
  global      = c(w = 50.850, h = 51.892),
  compartment = c(w = 30.648, h = 22.437)
)
VOLCANO_GLOBAL_LABELS <- c("Global_AllCompartments")

VOLCANO_FONT_FAMILY <- "Arial"
VOLCANO_FONT_PT     <- 6

VOLCANO_MINOR_STEP    <- 1
VOLCANO_STEP_SET      <- c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100)
VOLCANO_Y_MM_PER_TICK <- 5.0
VOLCANO_X_MM_PER_TICK <- 5.5
VOLCANO_TICK_MAJOR_MM <- 1.0
VOLCANO_TICK_MINOR_MM <- 0.55
VOLCANO_CANVAS_PAD_MM <- 1.0

# Optional y ceiling in -log10(padj) units. NULL = no cap, the standard. If
# set, genes above the ceiling are drawn AT the ceiling as filled triangles
# rather than dropped, and the count is written into the figure caption.
VOLCANO_Y_CAP <- NULL

# Thin the grey NS cloud for SVG file size. NULL keeps every point. Silent
# subsampling would misrepresent the figure, so this is off by default.
VOLCANO_MAX_NS <- NULL

# ---- matrisome masterlist ---------------------------------------------------
# The volcano is drawn ONCE, with the matrisome layer already on it. There is
# no separate matrisome replot chunk: plot_volcano takes matri_tbl and
# run_deg_gsea passes it, so the manuscript figure comes out of the first run.
MATRISOME_DIR     <- "Z:/Visium_Data/001_SpatialX"
MATRISOME_PAT     <- "^Mm_Matrisome_Masterlist.*\\.csv$"
MATRISOME_N_EACH  <- 10        # labelled genes per direction
MATRISOME_RANK_BY <- "lfc"     # "lfc" = largest fold change, "padj" = smallest padj

# Point colours, shared by the plain and the matrisome volcano so the two agree.
VOLC_COLS <- c("Up in Aged"  = "#B57BEE",
               "Up in Young" = "#007A7A",
               "NS"          = "grey70")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# load_matrisome: read the Naba masterlist and return gene / division / category.
# Column names are matched on a letters-only normalisation, so "Gene Symbol",
# "Gene.Symbol" and "gene symbol" all resolve.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
load_matrisome <- function(dir = MATRISOME_DIR, pattern = MATRISOME_PAT) {
  mfile <- list.files(dir, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(mfile)) {
    message("[WARN] no file matching ", pattern, " in ", dir,
            " - volcanoes will be drawn WITHOUT the matrisome layer")
    return(NULL)
  }
  if (length(mfile) > 1)
    message("[WARN] ", length(mfile), " matches; using ", basename(mfile[1]))
  mfile <- mfile[1]

  raw  <- read.csv(mfile, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  norm <- gsub("[^a-z]", "", tolower(names(raw)))
  pick <- function(key) {
    i <- which(norm == key); if (length(i)) names(raw)[i[1]] else NA_character_
  }
  gcol <- pick("genesymbol")
  dcol <- pick("matrisomedivision")
  ccol <- pick("matrisomecategory")
  if (is.na(gcol))
    stop("No 'Gene Symbol' column in ", basename(mfile), ". Columns: ",
         paste(names(raw), collapse = ", "))

  m <- data.frame(
    gene               = trimws(as.character(raw[[gcol]])),
    matrisome_division = if (!is.na(dcol)) as.character(raw[[dcol]]) else NA_character_,
    matrisome_category = if (!is.na(ccol)) as.character(raw[[ccol]]) else NA_character_,
    stringsAsFactors   = FALSE)
  m <- m[nzchar(m$gene) & !is.na(m$gene), , drop = FALSE]
  m <- m[!duplicated(m$gene), , drop = FALSE]

  message("Matrisome masterlist: ", basename(mfile), " -> ", nrow(m),
          " unique gene symbols")
  if (!is.na(dcol) && !is.na(ccol))
    print(table(m$matrisome_division, m$matrisome_category))
  m
}

# Ovary to animal. Six mice contributed a contralateral pair; four

OVARY_TO_ANIMAL <- c(

  "Y3" = "mY_16Sep24", "Y4" = "mY_16Sep24",

get_ovary_id <- function(tissue_slice) {
  sub("-[0-9]+$", "", as.character(tissue_slice))
}

get_animal_id <- function(tissue_slice) {
  ov  <- get_ovary_id(tissue_slice)
  out <- unname(OVARY_TO_ANIMAL[ov])
  if (any(is.na(out)))
    stop("Ovary not in OVARY_TO_ANIMAL: ",
         paste(unique(ov[is.na(out)]), collapse = ", "))
  out
}

pseudobulk <- function(counts_mat, meta, group_cols) {
  groups     <- do.call(paste, c(meta[group_cols], sep = "__"))
  unique_grp <- unique(groups)
  pb_list <- lapply(unique_grp, function(g) {
    cells <- which(groups == g)
    Matrix::rowSums(counts_mat[, cells, drop = FALSE])
  })
  pb_mat <- do.call(cbind, pb_list)
  colnames(pb_mat) <- unique_grp
  rownames(pb_mat) <- rownames(counts_mat)
  return(pb_mat)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# save_plot: every figure is written twice, PNG at FIG_DPI and SVG.
# out_base is a path WITHOUT an extension, so a caller cannot write a .png
# named .svg. svglite is preferred over grDevices::svg (no cairo dependency,
# smaller files, selectable text). If SVG fails the PNG is still written.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
save_plot <- function(p, out_base, width, height, dpi = FIG_DPI) {
  out_base <- sub("\\.(png|svg|pdf)$", "", out_base, ignore.case = TRUE)
  png_path <- paste0(out_base, ".png")
  svg_path <- paste0(out_base, ".svg")

  ggsave(png_path, p, width = width, height = height,
         units = "in", dpi = dpi, bg = "white")

  have_svglite <- requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE)
  svg_ok <- tryCatch({
    if (have_svglite) {
      ggsave(svg_path, p, width = width, height = height,
             units = "in", bg = "white", device = svglite::svglite)
    } else {
      ggsave(svg_path, p, width = width, height = height,
             units = "in", bg = "white", device = "svg")
    }
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("  SVG export failed (", conditionMessage(e),
            "). install.packages('svglite') is the usual fix.")
    FALSE
  })

  sz <- function(f) if (file.exists(f))
    paste0(round(file.size(f) / 1024), " KB") else "MISSING"
  message("  wrote ", basename(png_path), " (", sz(png_path), ")",
          if (svg_ok) paste0(" + ", basename(svg_path), " (", sz(svg_path), ")")
          else " ; SVG NOT written")
  invisible(c(png = png_path, svg = if (svg_ok) svg_path else NA_character_))
}

volcano_axis_ticks <- function(max_val,
                               panel_mm,
                               mm_per_tick = 5,
                               step_set    = VOLCANO_STEP_SET,
                               minor_step  = VOLCANO_MINOR_STEP,
                               force_step  = NULL,
                               force_limit = NULL) {

  if (!is.finite(max_val) || max_val <= 0) max_val <- 1
  max_ticks <- max(2, floor(panel_mm / mm_per_tick))

  if (!is.null(force_step)) {
    step  <- force_step
    limit <- if (!is.null(force_limit)) force_limit else
      ceiling(max_val / step) * step
  } else {
    cand <- lapply(step_set, function(s) {
      lim <- ceiling(max_val / s) * s
      list(step = s, limit = lim, n = lim / s)
    })
    cand <- Filter(function(x) x$n <= max_ticks, cand)
    if (!length(cand)) {
      step  <- step_set[which.min(abs(step_set - max_val))]
      limit <- ceiling(max_val / step) * step
    } else {
      lims  <- vapply(cand, function(x) x$limit, numeric(1))
      best  <- cand[[which.min(lims)]]
      step  <- best$step
      limit <- best$limit
    }
    if (!is.null(force_limit)) limit <- force_limit
  }

  major <- seq(0, limit, by = step)
  minor <- if (minor_step > 0 && minor_step < step)
    setdiff(seq(0, limit, by = minor_step), major) else numeric(0)

  list(limit = limit, step = step, major = major, minor = minor)
}

volcano_axis_ticks_sym <- function(max_abs, panel_mm, ...) {
  tk <- volcano_axis_ticks(max_abs, panel_mm = panel_mm / 2, ...)
  list(limit = tk$limit,
       step  = tk$step,
       major = sort(unique(c(-tk$major, tk$major))),
       minor = sort(unique(c(-tk$minor, tk$minor))))
}

fix_panel_size <- function(p, width_mm, height_mm) {
  g <- ggplot2::ggplotGrob(p)
  is_panel <- g$layout$name == "panel"
  if (!any(is_panel)) stop("fix_panel_size: no 'panel' cell in the gtable")
  g$widths[unique(g$layout$l[is_panel])]  <- grid::unit(width_mm,  "mm")
  g$heights[unique(g$layout$t[is_panel])] <- grid::unit(height_mm, "mm")
  g
}

grob_canvas_mm <- function(g, pad_mm = VOLCANO_CANVAS_PAD_MM) {
  opened <- FALSE
  if (is.null(grDevices::dev.list())) {
    grDevices::pdf(NULL, width = 20, height = 20)
    opened <- TRUE
  }
  on.exit(if (opened) grDevices::dev.off(), add = TRUE)
  w <- grid::convertWidth(sum(g$widths),   "mm", valueOnly = TRUE)
  h <- grid::convertHeight(sum(g$heights), "mm", valueOnly = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(w) || !is.finite(h))
    stop("grob_canvas_mm: could not resolve the gtable size to mm")
  c(w = w + pad_mm, h = h + pad_mm)
}

save_grob <- function(g, out_base, width_mm, height_mm, dpi = FIG_DPI) {
  out_base <- sub("\\.(png|svg|pdf)$", "", out_base, ignore.case = TRUE)
  png_path <- paste0(out_base, ".png")
  svg_path <- paste0(out_base, ".svg")
  w_in <- width_mm / 25.4
  h_in <- height_mm / 25.4

  if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) {
    ragg::agg_png(png_path, width = w_in, height = h_in, units = "in",
                  res = dpi, background = "white")
  } else {
    grDevices::png(png_path, width = w_in, height = h_in, units = "in",
                   res = dpi, bg = "white", type = "cairo")
  }
  grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(g); grDevices::dev.off()

  svg_ok <- tryCatch({
    if (requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE)) {
      svglite::svglite(svg_path, width = w_in, height = h_in, bg = "white")
    } else {
      grDevices::svg(svg_path, width = w_in, height = h_in, bg = "white")
    }
    grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(g); grDevices::dev.off()
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("  SVG export failed (", conditionMessage(e),
            "). install.packages('svglite') is the usual fix.")
    if (length(grDevices::dev.list())) try(grDevices::dev.off(), silent = TRUE)
    FALSE
  })

  sz <- function(f) if (file.exists(f))
    paste0(round(file.size(f) / 1024), " KB") else "MISSING"
  message("  wrote ", basename(png_path), " (", sz(png_path), ")",
          if (svg_ok) paste0(" + ", basename(svg_path), " (", sz(svg_path), ")")
          else " ; SVG NOT written",
          "  [canvas ", round(width_mm, 2), " x ", round(height_mm, 2), " mm]")
  invisible(c(png = png_path, svg = if (svg_ok) svg_path else NA_character_))
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# plot_volcano
#
# y = -log10(padj). The log is in the QUANTITY, not in the axis scale, which is
# why the ticks are evenly spaced at 0, 2.5, 5, 7.5. Each unit is one decade of
# padj: y = 0 is padj 1, y = 1.301 is padj 0.05, y = 5 is padj 1e-5. This is
# the universal volcano convention.
#
# x = log2FoldChange, symmetric limits so 0 sits at the centre of the panel.
#
# Thresholds are post-hoc. lfc_thr draws the two vertical lines and padj_thr
# the horizontal one; a gene is coloured only if it clears both. Negative LFC
# is "Up in Young", positive is "Up in Aged", so downregulation in Aged is
# never dropped, it is the teal half of the plot.
#
# MATRISOME LAYER
# Supply matri_tbl and every matrisome gene that is significant in EITHER
# direction is redrawn as shape 21 with a black rim, and the top n_each per
# direction are labelled. The colouring rule is identical either way, so the
# plain and the matrisome figure agree gene for gene. This used to be a
# separate replot chunk; it is folded in here so the first run produces the
# manuscript figure with no second pass. matri_tbl = NULL reproduces the
# original behaviour exactly, including the top-n_label-by-padj labelling.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_volcano <- function(res_df, title, out_base,
                         lfc_thr   = LFC_THRESHOLD,
                         padj_thr  = PADJ_CUTOFF,
                         n_label   = VOLCANO_N_LABEL,
                         lfc_col   = DEG_LFC_COL,
                         y_cap     = VOLCANO_Y_CAP,
                         scope     = c("auto", "global", "compartment"),
                         panel_w_mm = NULL,
                         panel_h_mm = NULL,
                         x_step    = NULL,
                         y_step    = NULL,
                         x_limit   = NULL,
                         y_limit   = NULL,
                         minor_step  = VOLCANO_MINOR_STEP,
                         font_pt     = VOLCANO_FONT_PT,
                         font_family = VOLCANO_FONT_FAMILY,
                         max_ns    = VOLCANO_MAX_NS,
                         matri_tbl = NULL,
                         n_each    = MATRISOME_N_EACH,
                         rank_by   = MATRISOME_RANK_BY,
                         write_gene_csv = TRUE) {

  if (!"padj" %in% names(res_df))
    stop("plot_volcano: 'padj' not in res_df")
  if (!lfc_col %in% names(res_df))
    stop("plot_volcano: column '", lfc_col, "' not in res_df")

  scope <- match.arg(scope)
  if (scope == "auto")
    scope <- if (any(vapply(VOLCANO_GLOBAL_LABELS,
                            function(k) grepl(k, out_base, fixed = TRUE),
                            logical(1)))) "global" else "compartment"
  pan <- VOLCANO_PANEL_MM[[scope]]
  if (is.null(panel_w_mm)) panel_w_mm <- unname(pan["w"])
  if (is.null(panel_h_mm)) panel_h_mm <- unname(pan["h"])

  df <- as.data.frame(res_df)
  df$lfc_plot <- df[[lfc_col]]
  df <- df[!is.na(df$padj) & !is.na(df$lfc_plot), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    message("  volcano: no finite points, skipped")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  # -log10(0) is Inf and ggplot would drop it silently. DESeq2 can return
  # padj == 0 through double underflow. Cap one decade below the smallest
  # non-zero value and report how many genes were affected.
  is_zero <- df$padj == 0
  if (any(is_zero)) {
    floor_p <- min(df$padj[!is_zero], na.rm = TRUE) / 10
    message("  volcano: ", sum(is_zero), " gene(s) with padj == 0, ",
            "capped at ", signif(floor_p, 3))
    df$padj[is_zero] <- floor_p
  }

  df$neg_log10_padj <- -log10(df$padj)
  df$sig <- dplyr::case_when(
    df$padj < padj_thr & df$lfc_plot >=  lfc_thr ~ "Up in Aged",
    df$padj < padj_thr & df$lfc_plot <= -lfc_thr ~ "Up in Young",
    TRUE                                        ~ "NS")

  # Sanity check. Under H0: LFC = 0 only a handful of genes should land at
  # padj == 1. A large count here means a threshold test crept back in.
  n_at_zero <- sum(df$neg_log10_padj == 0)
  if (n_at_zero > 0.02 * nrow(df))
    message("  [WARN] volcano: ", n_at_zero, " of ", nrow(df),
            " genes at padj == 1 exactly. Expect a flat line at y = 0. ",
            "Check that results() was called without lfcThreshold.")

  # Optional y ceiling: keep the points, move them to the cap, mark them.
  df$capped <- FALSE
  if (!is.null(y_cap)) {
    df$capped <- df$neg_log10_padj > y_cap
    if (any(df$capped)) {
      message("  volcano: ", sum(df$capped), " gene(s) above y = ", y_cap,
              " drawn AT the cap as triangles")
      df$neg_log10_padj[df$capped] <- y_cap
    }
  }

  message("  volcano: ", sum(df$sig == "Up in Aged"), " up in Aged, ",
          sum(df$sig == "Up in Young"), " up in Young ",
          "(padj < ", padj_thr, ", |", lfc_col, "| > ", lfc_thr, ")")

  n_ns <- sum(df$sig == "NS")
  if (!is.null(max_ns) && n_ns > max_ns) {
    set.seed(1)
    drop_idx <- sample(which(df$sig == "NS"), n_ns - max_ns)
    df <- df[-drop_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    message("  volcano: NS points thinned ", n_ns, " -> ", max_ns,
            ". THIS FIGURE IS SUBSAMPLED.")
  }

  # ---- matrisome selection ---------------------------------------------------
  use_matri <- !is.null(matri_tbl) && nrow(as.data.frame(matri_tbl)) > 0
  cand <- df[0, , drop = FALSE]
  if (use_matri) {
    if (!"gene" %in% names(df))
      stop("plot_volcano: matri_tbl supplied but res_df has no 'gene' column")
    df$is_matrisome <- df$gene %in% matri_tbl$gene
    message("  matrisome genes in tested universe: ", sum(df$is_matrisome),
            " of ", nrow(matri_tbl))
    cand <- df[df$is_matrisome & df$sig != "NS", , drop = FALSE]
    if (!nrow(cand)) {
      message("  no significant matrisome genes; drawn without the ",
              "matrisome layer")
      use_matri <- FALSE
    } else {
      message("  outlined: ", nrow(cand), "  (",
              sum(cand$sig == "Up in Aged"), " up in Aged, ",
              sum(cand$sig == "Up in Young"), " up in Young)")
    }
  }

  # ---- which genes get a text label ------------------------------------------
  if (use_matri) {
    # top n_each per direction among the OUTLINED genes, by |LFC| or by padj
    ord_val <- if (rank_by == "padj") cand$padj else -abs(cand$lfc_plot)
    cand <- cand[order(cand$sig, ord_val), , drop = FALSE]
    top_genes <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(cand, cand$sig),
                                       function(s) head(s, n_each)))
    message("  labelling ", nrow(top_genes), " matrisome genes, ranked by ",
            if (rank_by == "padj") "padj" else "|log2FC|")
  } else {
    # Label the strongest genes on BOTH sides, not simply the smallest padj,
    # which would otherwise fill every label slot from whichever direction
    # happens to be more significant.
    top_genes <- df %>%
      dplyr::filter(sig != "NS") %>%
      dplyr::group_by(sig) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(padj, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
      dplyr::slice_head(n = ceiling(n_label / 2)) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup()
  }

  x_tk <- volcano_axis_ticks_sym(
    max_abs     = max(abs(df$lfc_plot), na.rm = TRUE),
    panel_mm    = panel_w_mm,
    mm_per_tick = VOLCANO_X_MM_PER_TICK,
    minor_step  = minor_step,
    force_step  = x_step,
    force_limit = x_limit)

  y_max <- if (is.null(y_cap)) max(df$neg_log10_padj, na.rm = TRUE) else y_cap
  y_tk <- volcano_axis_ticks(
    max_val     = y_max,
    panel_mm    = panel_h_mm,
    mm_per_tick = VOLCANO_Y_MM_PER_TICK,
    minor_step  = minor_step,
    force_step  = y_step,
    force_limit = y_limit)

  message("  axes: x -", x_tk$limit, " to ", x_tk$limit, " by ", x_tk$step,
          " | y 0 to ", y_tk$limit, " by ", y_tk$step,
          " | minor ", if (minor_step > 0) minor_step else "off",
          " | panel ", round(panel_w_mm, 3), " x ", round(panel_h_mm, 3),
          " mm (", scope, ")")

  # background layers exclude the outlined genes so nothing is drawn twice
  df_ns  <- df[df$sig == "NS", , drop = FALSE]
  df_sig <- if (use_matri)
    df[df$sig != "NS" & !df$gene %in% cand$gene, , drop = FALSE] else
    df[df$sig != "NS", , drop = FALSE]

  cap_note <- if (!is.null(y_cap) && any(df$capped))
    paste0(sum(df$capped), " gene(s) capped at y = ", y_cap,
           " (triangles)") else NULL
  matri_note <- if (use_matri)
    paste0(nrow(cand), " matrisome DEGs outlined; top ", n_each,
           " per direction labelled by ",
           if (rank_by == "padj") "padj" else "|log2FC|") else NULL
  caption <- paste(na.omit(c(matri_note, cap_note)), collapse = "; ")
  if (!nzchar(caption)) caption <- NULL

  chars_per_line <- max(16, floor(panel_w_mm / (0.55 * font_pt * 0.3528)))
  title_wrapped  <- paste(strwrap(title, width = chars_per_line),
                          collapse = "\n")
  if (!is.null(caption))
    caption <- paste(strwrap(caption, width = chars_per_line), collapse = "\n")

  label_size_mm <- font_pt / .pt

  has_minor <- utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "3.5.0"
  if (!has_minor && minor_step > 0)
    message("  [NOTE] ggplot2 ", as.character(utils::packageVersion("ggplot2")),
            " has no guide_axis(minor.ticks=); minor ticks omitted.")

  p <- ggplot(mapping = aes(x = lfc_plot, y = neg_log10_padj)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-lfc_thr, lfc_thr),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(padj_thr),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.25) +
    # NS underneath, significant on top, so colour is never hidden
    geom_point(data = df_ns,  aes(colour = sig, shape = capped),
               size = 0.45, alpha = 0.45, stroke = 0) +
    geom_point(data = df_sig, aes(colour = sig, shape = capped),
               size = 0.65, alpha = 0.85, stroke = 0)

  if (use_matri)
    # shape 21 takes the fill inside and a black rim outside
    p <- p + geom_point(data = cand, aes(fill = sig),
                        shape = 21, size = 0.85, stroke = 0.18,
                        colour = "black")

  p <- p +
    geom_text_repel(data = top_genes, aes(label = gene, colour = sig),
                    family = font_family, size = label_size_mm,
                    fontface = if (use_matri) "bold" else "plain",
                    max.overlaps = if (use_matri) 40 else 20, seed = 42,
                    box.padding = if (use_matri) 0.22 else 0.18,
                    point.padding = if (use_matri) 0.15 else 0.12,
                    min.segment.length = 0.2, segment.size = 0.2,
                    segment.colour = "grey45", show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = VOLC_COLS,
                        breaks = c("Up in Young", "NS", "Up in Aged")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = VOLC_COLS, guide = "none") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 17), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_tk$major, minor_breaks = x_tk$minor) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = y_tk$major, minor_breaks = y_tk$minor) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-x_tk$limit, x_tk$limit),
                    ylim = c(0, y_tk$limit),
                    expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
    labs(title   = title_wrapped,
         x       = "log2 fold change (Aged / Young)",
         y       = "-log10 adjusted p-value",
         colour  = NULL,
         caption = caption) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1,
                                 override.aes = list(size = 1.6, alpha = 1)))

  if (has_minor && minor_step > 0)
    p <- p + guides(x = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE),
                    y = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE))

  p <- p +
    theme_classic(base_size = font_pt, base_family = font_family) +
    theme(text              = element_text(family = font_family,
                                           size = font_pt),
          plot.title        = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold",
                                           size = font_pt),
          plot.caption      = element_text(size = font_pt, colour = "grey35",
                                           hjust = 0.5),
          axis.title        = element_text(size = font_pt),
          axis.text         = element_text(size = font_pt, colour = "black"),
          axis.line         = element_line(linewidth = 0.25, colour = "black"),
          axis.ticks        = element_line(linewidth = 0.25, colour = "black"),
          axis.ticks.length = grid::unit(VOLCANO_TICK_MAJOR_MM, "mm"),
          legend.position   = "top",
          legend.text       = element_text(size = font_pt),
          legend.key.size   = grid::unit(2.2, "mm"),
          legend.margin     = margin(b = -2),
          plot.margin       = margin(1, 2, 1, 1, unit = "mm"))

  if (has_minor && minor_step > 0)
    p <- p + theme(axis.minor.ticks.length =
                     grid::unit(VOLCANO_TICK_MINOR_MM, "mm"))

  g   <- fix_panel_size(p, width_mm = panel_w_mm, height_mm = panel_h_mm)
  cvs <- grob_canvas_mm(g)
  save_grob(g, out_base, width_mm = cvs["w"], height_mm = cvs["h"])

  # the exact genes behind the outlined layer, for the figure legend
  if (use_matri && write_gene_csv) {
    out <- merge(cand, matri_tbl, by = "gene", all.x = TRUE)
    out$labelled <- out$gene %in% top_genes$gene
    want <- c("gene", "sig", "labelled", lfc_col, "padj", "pval",
              "matrisome_division", "matrisome_category")
    out <- out[order(out$sig, -abs(out$lfc_plot)),
               want[want %in% names(out)], drop = FALSE]
    write.csv(out, paste0(sub("\\.(png|svg|pdf)$", "", out_base), "_genes.csv"),
              row.names = FALSE)
  }
  return(invisible(p))
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# tidy_pathway: MSigDB names are SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE with a collection prefix.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
tidy_pathway <- function(x, max_chars = 48) {
  y <- sub("^(HALLMARK|GOBP|GOCC|GOMF|REACTOME|WP|KEGG|BIOCARTA|PID)_", "", x)
  y <- tolower(gsub("_", " ", y))
  y <- paste0(toupper(substr(y, 1, 1)), substr(y, 2, nchar(y)))
  ifelse(nchar(y) > max_chars, paste0(substr(y, 1, max_chars - 3), "..."), y)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# plot_gsea_dot
#   x        = NES (negative = enriched in Young, positive = enriched in Aged)
#   y        = pathway
#   dot size = number of genes from the pathway present in the ranking
#   colour   = statistical significance, -log10(padj)
#
# n_top LIMITS THE DRAWING ONLY. It selects how many pathway rows fit on the
# panel; it has no effect on the enrichment test, which has already run over
# every gene set. The full result, every pathway with its NES and padj, is in
# GSEA_<label>_Aged_vs_Young.csv. Raise n_top or filter the CSV yourself if
# you want more rows.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_gsea_dot <- function(gsea_res, title, out_base, n_top = 20,
                          padj_thr = 0.05,
                          independent_only = TRUE,
                          width = GSEA_DOT_W) {
  # fgsea returns a data.table; `$<-` on a data.table triggers shallow-copy
  # warnings in some versions, so work on a plain data.frame here
  df <- as.data.frame(gsea_res) %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj), padj < padj_thr)

  if (independent_only && "independent" %in% names(df) &&
      any(df$independent %in% TRUE)) {
    n_before <- nrow(df)
    df <- dplyr::filter(df, independent %in% TRUE)
    message("  dotplot: ", nrow(df), " independent of ", n_before,
            " significant pathways")
  }
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    message("  No significant GSEA pathways at padj < ", padj_thr)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  if (!"size" %in% names(df))
    stop("plot_gsea_dot: fgsea 'size' column missing")

  # take the strongest from each direction so the panel is not one-sided
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dir = ifelse(NES > 0, "Aged", "Young")) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dir) %>%
    dplyr::slice_max(order_by = abs(NES), n = ceiling(n_top / 2),
                     with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pathway_label  = tidy_pathway(pathway),
                  neg_log10_padj = -log10(padj)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(NES)
  # truncation can collide two long names; make them distinct before factoring
  df$pathway_label <- make.unique(df$pathway_label, sep = " ")
  df$pathway_label <- factor(df$pathway_label, levels = df$pathway_label)

  x_abs <- max(abs(df$NES), na.rm = TRUE)

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = NES, y = pathway_label)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
               colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = NES,
                     y = pathway_label, yend = pathway_label),
                 colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_point(aes(size = size, fill = neg_log10_padj),
                 shape = 21, colour = "black", stroke = 0.25) +
    # fill is the mapped aesthetic (shape 21), so the scale must be a FILL
    # scale. A colour scale here applies to nothing and ggplot silently falls
    # back to its default blue fill gradient. Same viridis settings as the
    # curated manuscript dot plot, so the automatic and the curated figure are
    # visually interchangeable.
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C", direction = 1, begin = 0.05, end = 1,
                         name = expression(-log[10]~italic(p)[adj])) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 6), name = "Genes in set") +
    guides(size = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21,
                                                   fill = "grey70",
                                                   colour = "black"))) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-x_abs, x_abs) * 1.08,
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    labs(title = paste(strwrap(title, width = 60), collapse = "\n"),
         x     = "Normalised Enrichment Score (NES)",
         y     = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
    theme(plot.title      = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 10),
          axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 7),
          axis.text.x     = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.position = "right",
          legend.title    = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.text     = element_text(size = 7),
          legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.35, "cm"),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey93",
                                            linewidth = 0.2))

  save_plot(p, out_base,
            width  = width,
            height = max(3.2, 0.24 * nrow(df) + 1.7))
  return(invisible(p))
}

# =============================================================================
# CORE DEG + GSEA RUNNER
# =============================================================================

summarise_leading_edge <- function(gsea_res, label, out_base,
                                   padj_thr = 0.05,
                                   jaccard  = GSEA_LE_JACCARD) {
  if (!"leadingEdge" %in% names(gsea_res)) {
    message("  leadingEdge absent; skipped"); return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  sig <- as.data.frame(gsea_res)
  le  <- gsea_res$leadingEdge
  keep <- !is.na(sig$padj) & sig$padj < padj_thr
  sig <- sig[keep, , drop = FALSE]; le <- le[keep]
  if (nrow(sig) == 0) {
    message("  no significant pathways; skipped"); return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  ord <- order(sig$padj); sig <- sig[ord, , drop = FALSE]; le <- le[ord]

  n <- nrow(sig); cluster <- rep(NA_integer_, n); k <- 0L
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (!is.na(cluster[i])) next
    k <- k + 1L; cluster[i] <- k
    if (i < n) for (j in (i + 1):n) {
      if (!is.na(cluster[j])) next
      a <- le[[i]]; b <- le[[j]]; u <- length(union(a, b))
      if (u > 0 && length(intersect(a, b)) / u >= jaccard) cluster[j] <- k
    }
  }

  summ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(k), function(cc) {
    idx <- which(cluster == cc); mem <- le[idx]
    all_g <- unlist(mem); tab <- table(all_g)
    core <- names(tab)[tab >= max(1, ceiling(length(idx) / 2))]
    data.frame(le_cluster = cc, n_pathways = length(idx),
               representative = sig$pathway[idx[1]],
               rep_padj = sig$padj[idx[1]], rep_NES = sig$NES[idx[1]],
               direction = sig$direction[idx[1]],
               collections = paste(sort(unique(sig$collection[idx])),
                                   collapse = "/"),
               n_union_genes = length(unique(all_g)),
               n_core_genes = length(core),
               core_genes = paste(head(core, 40), collapse = "|"),
               member_pathways = paste(sig$pathway[idx], collapse = "|"),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  summ <- summ[order(-summ$n_pathways, summ$rep_padj), ]
  write.csv(summ, file.path(out_base,
            paste0("GSEA_leadingEdge_clusters_", label, ".csv")),
            row.names = FALSE)

  message("  ", label, ": ", k, " distinct signals behind ", n,
          " significant pathways")
  top <- head(summ, 3)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(top)))
    message(sprintf("    [%3d pathways] %-44s NES %+0.2f %s",
                    top$n_pathways[i],
                    substr(tidy_pathway(top$representative[i], 44), 1, 44),
                    top$rep_NES[i], top$direction[i]))
  invisible(summ)
}

run_deg_gsea <- function(seu, meta, test_def, gene_sets,
                          out_base, lfc_thr, padj_thr,
                          min_cells) {
  label      <- test_def$label
  filter_col <- test_def$filter_col
  filter_vals <- test_def$filter_vals

  message("\n", paste(rep("-", 50), collapse = ""))
  message("Test: ", label,
          "  [", filter_col, " == ", paste(filter_vals, collapse = "/"), "]")

  cell_mask  <- meta[[filter_col]] %in% filter_vals & !is.na(meta[[filter_col]])
  test_cells <- rownames(meta)[cell_mask]

  if (length(test_cells) < 50) {
    message("  SKIPPED: fewer than 50 bins (n = ", length(test_cells), ")")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  message("  Bins: ", length(test_cells))

  seu_sub   <- subset(seu, cells = test_cells)
  meta_sub  <- seu_sub@meta.data
  meta_sub$animal_id <- get_animal_id(meta_sub[[TSV_TISSUE_COL]])
  meta_sub$age_group <- ifelse(
    grepl("Young", meta_sub[[TSV_AGE_COL]], ignore.case = TRUE),
    "Young", "Aged")

  bin_tbl <- meta_sub %>%
    group_by(animal_id, age_group) %>%
    summarise(n_bins = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(age_group, animal_id)
  message("  Bin counts per animal:")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(bin_tbl))) {
    message(sprintf("    %-10s  %-6s  %d bins",
                    bin_tbl$animal_id[i],
                    bin_tbl$age_group[i],
                    bin_tbl$n_bins[i]))
  }

  counts <- LayerData(seu_sub, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  pb_mat  <- pseudobulk(counts, meta_sub,
                         group_cols = c("animal_id", "age_group"))

  pb_meta <- data.frame(
    sample    = colnames(pb_mat),
    animal_id = sub("__.*", "", colnames(pb_mat)),
    age_group = sub(".*__", "", colnames(pb_mat)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  cell_counts   <- table(
    paste(meta_sub$animal_id, meta_sub$age_group, sep = "__"))
  pb_meta$n_bins <- as.integer(cell_counts[pb_meta$sample])

  keep    <- !is.na(pb_meta$n_bins) & pb_meta$n_bins >= min_cells
  pb_mat  <- pb_mat[, keep, drop = FALSE]
  pb_meta <- pb_meta[keep, ]

  n_young <- sum(pb_meta$age_group == "Young")
  n_aged  <- sum(pb_meta$age_group == "Aged")
  message("  Pseudobulk samples after filter: Young=", n_young,
          "  Aged=", n_aged)

  if (n_young < 2 || n_aged < 2) {
    message("  SKIPPED: need >=2 pseudobulk samples per group. ",
            "Consider lowering MIN_CELLS_PER_SAMPLE or interpret with caution.")
    write.csv(bin_tbl,
              file.path(out_base, paste0("BinCounts_", label, ".csv")),
              row.names = FALSE)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  keep_genes  <- rowSums(pb_mat > MIN_COUNT_PER_SAMPLE) >= MIN_SAMPLES_DETECTED
  pb_mat_filt <- pb_mat[keep_genes, ]
  message("  Genes after count filter (>", MIN_COUNT_PER_SAMPLE, " in >=",
          MIN_SAMPLES_DETECTED, " of ", ncol(pb_mat), " samples): ",
          nrow(pb_mat_filt))

  pb_meta$age_group <- factor(pb_meta$age_group, levels = c("Young", "Aged"))

  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    countData = round(pb_mat_filt),
    colData   = pb_meta,
    design    = ~ age_group)
  dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds)
  dds <- DESeq(dds, test = "Wald", fitType = "parametric", quiet = TRUE)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Ordinary two-sided Wald test, H0: log2FoldChange = 0. No lfcThreshold, no
  # altHypothesis. Genes higher in Young get a negative LFC and genes higher in
  # Aged a positive one; both are tested and both appear in the output. The
  # |LFC| > 1 and padj < 0.05 rules are applied afterwards, when plotting and
  # counting, so they can be changed without refitting.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  res <- results(dds,
                 contrast = c("age_group", "Aged", "Young"),
                 alpha    = padj_thr)

  # apeglm shrinks the LFC for low-count genes. It requires the coef name
  # rather than a contrast, and it drops the Wald 'stat' column, so the two
  # frames are selected and renamed explicitly rather than joined by suffix.
  coef_name <- resultsNames(dds)[grepl("age_group", resultsNames(dds))]
  res_shrunk <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = coef_name, type = "apeglm", quiet = TRUE)

  res_shr_df <- as.data.frame(res_shrunk) %>%
    rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
    dplyr::select(gene, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE)

  res_std_df <- as.data.frame(res) %>%
    rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
    dplyr::select(gene,
                  log2FoldChange_mle = log2FoldChange,
                  lfcSE_mle          = lfcSE,
                  stat, pvalue, padj)

  # log2FoldChange      apeglm posterior estimate, plotted on x
  # log2FoldChange_mle  unshrunken MLE, the quantity the Wald test tested
  # stat                Wald statistic, used to rank genes for GSEA
  # padj                BH adjusted Wald p-value, plotted on y
  res_df <- res_shr_df %>%
    dplyr::left_join(res_std_df, by = "gene") %>%
    arrange(padj)

  lfc_for_call <- res_df[[DEG_LFC_COL]]
  n_up <- sum(res_df$padj < padj_thr & lfc_for_call >=  lfc_thr, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_dn <- sum(res_df$padj < padj_thr & lfc_for_call <= -lfc_thr, na.rm = TRUE)
  message("  DEGs (padj < ", padj_thr, " & |", DEG_LFC_COL, "| > ", lfc_thr,
          "): ", n_up, " up in Aged, ", n_dn, " up in Young")
  message("  padj < ", padj_thr, " regardless of LFC: ",
          sum(res_df$padj < padj_thr, na.rm = TRUE))

  write.csv(res_df,
            file.path(out_base, paste0("DEG_", label, "_Aged_vs_Young.csv")),
            row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(bin_tbl,
            file.path(out_base, paste0("BinCounts_", label, ".csv")),
            row.names = FALSE)
  if (isTRUE(SAVE_DDS))
    saveRDS(dds, file.path(out_base, paste0("dds_", label, ".rds")))

  # Plain volcano, then the same figure with the matrisome layer. Both come out
  # of this single run; there is no replot pass. matrisome_tbl is created by the
  # data chunk and is NULL if the masterlist was not found, in which case the
  # second call silently produces the plain figure again.
  plot_volcano(res_df,
    title    = paste0(label, ": Aged vs Young (DESeq2 pseudobulk)"),
    out_base = file.path(out_base,
                         paste0("Volcano_", label, "_Aged_vs_Young")),
    lfc_thr  = lfc_thr,
    padj_thr = padj_thr)

  if (exists("matrisome_tbl") && !is.null(matrisome_tbl))
    plot_volcano(res_df,
      title     = paste0(label, ": matrisome, Aged vs Young"),
      out_base  = file.path(out_base,
                            paste0("Volcano-matrisome_", label,
                                   "_Aged_vs_Young")),
      lfc_thr   = lfc_thr,
      padj_thr  = padj_thr,
      matri_tbl = matrisome_tbl)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # GSEA operates on the COMPLETE ranked gene list, not on a DEG subset. Every
  # gene that survived the pseudobulk count filter goes into rank_vec, ordered
  # by the signed Wald statistic. That is what distinguishes GSEA from an
  # over-representation test: it detects a coordinated shift in a gene set even
  # when no individual member clears padj < 0.05 or |LFC| > 1.
  #
  # Consequently LFC_THRESHOLD and PADJ_CUTOFF do not enter GSEA at all.
  # Changing them changes the volcano and the DEG list; it leaves every NES and
  # every GSEA padj identical.
  #
  # If you want an enrichment test that DOES respect the threshold, that is
  # over-representation analysis on the DEG list, a different question with a
  # different null. The optional {r ORA-from-DEG} chunk at the end runs it.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  rank_df <- res_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(stat), is.finite(stat)) %>%
    dplyr::select(gene, stat)
  if (any(duplicated(rank_df$gene)))
    stop("Duplicate gene symbols in the ranking vector for test ", label)
  rank_vec <- deframe(rank_df)

  message("  GSEA ranking: ", length(rank_vec), " genes; ",
          sum(rank_vec == 0), " exactly 0; range ",
          paste(signif(range(rank_vec), 3), collapse = " to "))
  if (sum(rank_vec == 0) > 0.1 * length(rank_vec))
    message("  [WARN] more than 10% of the ranking is tied at 0.")

  set.seed(42)
  gsea_res <- fgsea(pathways    = gene_sets,
                     stats       = rank_vec,
                     minSize     = GSEA_MIN_SIZE,
                     maxSize     = GSEA_MAX_SIZE,
                     nPermSimple = GSEA_NPERM)
  
  if (nrow(gsea_res) == 0) {
    message("  no gene set inside the size window ", GSEA_MIN_SIZE,
            " to ", GSEA_MAX_SIZE, "; nothing tested")
    return(list(deg = res_df, gsea = data.frame(
      pathway = character(0), pval = numeric(0), padj = numeric(0),
      ES = numeric(0), NES = numeric(0), size = integer(0),
      direction = character(0), collection = character(0),
      independent = logical(0), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
  }
  
  gsea_res <- gsea_res %>%
    arrange(padj) %>%
    mutate(direction = ifelse(NES > 0, "Up in Aged", "Up in Young"))

  gsea_res$collection <- unname(gene_set_source[gsea_res$pathway])

  # GO:BP is deeply nested, so a parent term and its children fire together.
  # collapsePathways flags a non-redundant subset. Nothing is discarded: the
  # CSV keeps every pathway, with independent = TRUE on the retained ones.
  gsea_res$independent <- NA
  sig_dt <- data.table::as.data.table(gsea_res)[padj < 0.05][order(pval)]
  if (nrow(sig_dt) > 1) {
    keep <- tryCatch(
      fgsea::collapsePathways(sig_dt, gene_sets, rank_vec)$mainPathways,
      error = function(e) {
        message("  collapsePathways failed (", conditionMessage(e),
                "); leaving independent = NA")
        NULL
      })
    if (!is.null(keep)) {
      gsea_res$independent <- gsea_res$pathway %in% keep
      message("  Independent pathways after collapsing: ", length(keep),
              " of ", nrow(sig_dt), " significant")
    }
  }

  gsea_out <- as.data.frame(gsea_res)
  gsea_out$leadingEdge <- vapply(gsea_res$leadingEdge,
                                 function(v) paste(v, collapse = "|"),
                                 character(1))
  write.csv(gsea_out,
            file.path(out_base, paste0("GSEA_", label, "_Aged_vs_Young.csv")),
            row.names = FALSE)

  summarise_leading_edge(gsea_res, label, out_base)

  message("  Significant GSEA pathways (padj<0.05): ",
          sum(gsea_res$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
          "  (", sum(gsea_res$padj < 0.05 & gsea_res$NES > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
          " up in Aged, ",
          sum(gsea_res$padj < 0.05 & gsea_res$NES < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
          " up in Young)")

  plot_gsea_dot(gsea_res,
    title    = paste0(label, ": GSEA Aged vs Young"),
    out_base = file.path(out_base,
                         paste0("GSEA_dotplot_", label, "_Aged_vs_Young")))

  return(list(deg = res_df, gsea = gsea_res))
}

# =============================================================================
# CROSS-TEST SUMMARY, factored out so any chunk can rebuild it
# =============================================================================

write_cross_test_summaries <- function(all_results, output_dir) {
  if (length(all_results) == 0) {
    message("No results to summarise.")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  message("Tests in all_results: ", paste(names(all_results), collapse = ", "))

  # all_results lives for the whole R session. A result computed under an older
  # version of this config chunk therefore survives a re-run of the test loop
  # and lands here with a different column set, which used to abort the summary
  # with "Column `log2FoldChange_mle` doesn't exist". Drop such entries by name
  # rather than failing, so the tests that ARE current still get summarised.
  .needed_deg <- c("gene", "baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "log2FoldChange_mle",
                   "pvalue", "padj")
  .ok <- vapply(all_results, function(r) {
    !is.null(r$deg) && all(.needed_deg %in% names(r$deg))
  }, logical(1))
  if (any(!.ok)) {
    message("[STALE, DROPPED] computed under an older config: ",
            paste(names(all_results)[!.ok], collapse = ", "))
    message("  Re-run those tests to include them in the summary.")
    all_results <- all_results[.ok]
  }
  if (length(all_results) == 0) {
    message("Nothing current left to summarise.")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  deg_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(all_results), function(lbl) {
    d <- all_results[[lbl]]$deg
    d$lfc_call <- d[[DEG_LFC_COL]]
    d %>%
      filter(padj < PADJ_CUTOFF, abs(lfc_call) >= LFC_THRESHOLD) %>%
      mutate(test      = lbl,
             direction = ifelse(lfc_call > 0, "Up_Aged", "Up_Young")) %>%
      dplyr::select(test, gene, baseMean, log2FoldChange, log2FoldChange_mle,
                    pvalue, padj, direction)
  }))
  write.csv(deg_summary, file.path(output_dir, "DEG_summary_all_tests.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  message("DEG summary rows: ", nrow(deg_summary),
          "  (", sum(deg_summary$direction == "Up_Aged"), " Up_Aged, ",
          sum(deg_summary$direction == "Up_Young"), " Up_Young)")

  gsea_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(all_results), function(lbl) {
    all_results[[lbl]]$gsea %>%
      filter(padj < 0.05) %>%
      mutate(test = lbl) %>%
      dplyr::select(test, pathway, NES, padj, direction,
                    dplyr::any_of(c("size", "collection", "independent")))
  }))
  write.csv(gsea_summary, file.path(output_dir, "GSEA_summary_all_tests.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  shared <- gsea_summary %>%
    group_by(pathway) %>%
    summarise(n_tests    = n_distinct(test),
              tests      = paste(test, collapse = ", "),
              mean_NES   = mean(NES),
              consistent = n_distinct(direction) == 1,
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n_tests >= 2) %>%
    arrange(desc(n_tests), desc(abs(mean_NES)))
  write.csv(shared,
            file.path(output_dir, "GSEA_shared_pathways_across_tests.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  message("Shared pathways (>=2 tests): ", nrow(shared))
  invisible(list(deg = deg_summary, gsea = gsea_summary, shared = shared))
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# rebuild_summaries_from_csv: same three summary tables, but read back from the
# DEG_*.csv / GSEA_*.csv already on disk instead of from `all_results` in
# memory. This is what makes a threshold change a replot-only operation: the
# per-gene statistics never change, so re-applying LFC_THRESHOLD and
# PADJ_CUTOFF to the saved files reproduces the summaries without refitting.
# Files written before CONFIG_VERSION 2026-08-05_v3 are skipped, not silently
# re-thresholded, because their padj came from a different null.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
rebuild_summaries_from_csv <- function(root_dir, output_dir = OUTPUT_DIR) {
  deg_files <- list.files(root_dir, pattern = "^DEG_.*_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$",
                          recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  gsea_files <- list.files(root_dir, pattern = "^GSEA_.*_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$",
                           recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  message("Rebuilding summaries from ", length(deg_files), " DEG and ",
          length(gsea_files), " GSEA CSVs in ", root_dir)

  deg_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(deg_files, function(f) {
    d   <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    lbl <- sub("^DEG_(.*)_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$", "\\1", basename(f))
    if (!"log2FoldChange_mle" %in% names(d) || "padj_lfcthr" %in% names(d)) {
      message("  [STALE, SKIPPED] ", basename(f))
      return(NULL)
    }
    d$lfc_call <- d[[DEG_LFC_COL]]
    d %>%
      filter(!is.na(padj), padj < PADJ_CUTOFF,
             abs(lfc_call) >= LFC_THRESHOLD) %>%
      mutate(test      = lbl,
             direction = ifelse(lfc_call > 0, "Up_Aged", "Up_Young")) %>%
      dplyr::select(test, gene, baseMean, log2FoldChange, log2FoldChange_mle,
                    pvalue, padj, direction)
  }))
  write.csv(deg_summary, file.path(output_dir, "DEG_summary_all_tests.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  message("  DEG summary rows: ", nrow(deg_summary),
          "  (padj < ", PADJ_CUTOFF, ", |", DEG_LFC_COL, "| > ",
          LFC_THRESHOLD, ")")
  if (nrow(deg_summary) > 0)
    print(table(deg_summary$test, deg_summary$direction))

  gsea_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(gsea_files, function(f) {
    g   <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    lbl <- sub("^GSEA_(.*)_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$", "\\1", basename(f))
    if (!all(c("pathway", "NES", "padj") %in% names(g))) return(NULL)
    g %>%
      filter(!is.na(padj), padj < 0.05) %>%
      mutate(test = lbl,
             direction = ifelse(NES > 0, "Up in Aged", "Up in Young")) %>%
      dplyr::select(test, pathway, NES, padj, direction,
                    dplyr::any_of(c("size", "collection", "independent")))
  }))
  write.csv(gsea_summary, file.path(output_dir, "GSEA_summary_all_tests.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  shared <- gsea_summary %>%
    group_by(pathway) %>%
    summarise(n_tests    = n_distinct(test),
              tests      = paste(test, collapse = ", "),
              mean_NES   = mean(NES),
              consistent = n_distinct(direction) == 1,
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n_tests >= 2) %>%
    arrange(desc(n_tests), desc(abs(mean_NES)))
  write.csv(shared,
            file.path(output_dir, "GSEA_shared_pathways_across_tests.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  message("  Shared pathways (>=2 tests): ", nrow(shared))

  invisible(list(deg = deg_summary, gsea = gsea_summary, shared = shared))
}

# =============================================================================
# STALENESS GUARD
# Fails loudly if the session holds an older version of this config chunk,
# which is the exact failure mode of running a single chunk after editing.
# =============================================================================

assert_config_current <- function(expect_version = "2026-08-31_v1") {
  need_objs <- c("run_deg_gsea", "summarise_leading_edge", 
                 "plot_volcano", "plot_gsea_dot", "save_plot",
                 "write_cross_test_summaries", "rebuild_summaries_from_csv",
                 "tidy_pathway", "load_matrisome", "VOLC_COLS",
                 "MATRISOME_N_EACH", "MATRISOME_RANK_BY",
                 "GSEA_MIN_SIZE", "GSEA_MAX_SIZE", "GSEA_NPERM",
                 "LFC_THRESHOLD", "PADJ_CUTOFF", "DEG_LFC_COL",
                 "MIN_CELLS_PER_SAMPLE", "MIN_COUNT_PER_SAMPLE",
                 "MIN_SAMPLES_DETECTED", "OUTPUT_DIR", "FIG_DPI",
                 "VOLCANO_W", "VOLCANO_H")
  miss <- need_objs[!vapply(need_objs, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss))
    stop("Run the {r DEG-GSEA-config} chunk first. Missing: ",
         paste(miss, collapse = ", "))

  if (!exists("CONFIG_VERSION") || !identical(CONFIG_VERSION, expect_version))
    stop("Config in the session is version '",
         if (exists("CONFIG_VERSION")) CONFIG_VERSION else "<none>",
         "' but this chunk expects '", expect_version,
         "'. Re-run {r DEG-GSEA-config}.")

  # Signature checks: catch a stale definition that shares a name.
  if (!"out_base" %in% names(formals(plot_volcano)))
    stop("plot_volcano in this session is an OLD version (takes out_path). ",
         "Re-run {r DEG-GSEA-config}.")
  if (!"matri_tbl" %in% names(formals(plot_volcano)))
    stop("plot_volcano in this session predates the merged matrisome layer. ",
         "Re-run {r DEG-GSEA-config}.")
  body_txt <- paste(deparse(body(run_deg_gsea)), collapse = " ")
  if (grepl("lfcThreshold", body_txt))
    stop("run_deg_gsea in this session still calls results() with ",
         "lfcThreshold. Re-run {r DEG-GSEA-config}.")

  message("Config OK: ", CONFIG_VERSION,
          " | H0: LFC = 0 (two-sided Wald)",
          " | lines at |LFC| > ", LFC_THRESHOLD,
          " and padj < ", PADJ_CUTOFF,
          " | threshold applied to ", DEG_LFC_COL,
          " | volcano ", VOLCANO_W, " x ", VOLCANO_H, " in @ ", FIG_DPI,
          " dpi | svglite ",
          if (requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE)) "yes" else "NO")
  invisible(TRUE)
}

message("Config loaded: ", CONFIG_VERSION)
#```

# 3. Data: metadata merge, gene sets, matrisome

#```{r DEG-GSEA-data}
assert_config_current()

if (!exists("merge.full"))
  stop("merge.full not in the session. Run the export chunk, or readRDS it.")

message("\n=== Loading Seurat RDS ===")
seu <- merge.full

message("\n=== Loading metadata TSV ===")
tsv <- read.delim(METADATA_TSV, sep = "\t",
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)

required_cols <- c(TSV_BARCODE_COL, TSV_SAMPLE_COL,
                    TSV_CLUSTER_COL, TSV_AGE_COL, TSV_TISSUE_COL)
missing_cols  <- required_cols[!required_cols %in% colnames(tsv)]
if (length(missing_cols) > 0)
  stop("Missing TSV columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))

tsv$barcode_full <- paste0(tsv[[TSV_BARCODE_COL]], ".", tsv[[TSV_SAMPLE_COL]])
tsv_sub <- tsv[!duplicated(tsv$barcode_full),
                c("barcode_full", TSV_CLUSTER_COL,
                  TSV_AGE_COL, TSV_TISSUE_COL, "Compartments")]
rownames(tsv_sub) <- tsv_sub$barcode_full
tsv_sub$barcode_full <- NULL

n_overlap <- sum(rownames(tsv_sub) %in% colnames(seu))
message("Barcodes matched: ", n_overlap, " / ", nrow(tsv_sub))
if (n_overlap < 100)
  stop("Very few barcode matches — check format. ",
       "TSV: ", rownames(tsv_sub)[1],
       "  Seurat: ", colnames(seu)[1])

seu <- AddMetaData(seu, metadata = tsv_sub)

message("\nBins per compartment (from Compartments column):")
print(table(seu@meta.data[["Compartments"]], useNA = "ifany"))
message("\nBins per age group:")
print(table(seu@meta.data[[TSV_AGE_COL]], useNA = "ifany"))

meta <- seu@meta.data

# =============================================================================
# LOAD GENE SETS
# db_species = "MM" reads the mouse-native MSigDB (2026.1.Mm) directly, with no
# human-to-mouse ortholog mapping. The mouse database has NO KEGG collection,
# so Reactome replaces the CP:KEGG sets used previously.
# Collections are M-prefixed: MH = Hallmark, M2 = curated, M5 = GO.
#
# ALL FIVE COLLECTIONS ARE LOADED HERE. GO:CC and GO:MF used to be added by a
# separate re-run chunk that overwrote the GSEA CSVs afterwards; they are loaded
# up front instead, so the first run tests the family the curation was built on.
# This matters for more than convenience: BH correction is applied across the
# whole tested family, so the padj of a Hallmark set depends on how many GO sets
# were tested alongside it. Loading all five at once is the only way the padj in
# the figures and the padj in the curated tables are the same number.
# =============================================================================

message("\n=== Loading MSigDB gene sets (mouse-native) ===")

GSEA_COLLECTIONS <- list(
  list(coll = "MH", sub = NULL,          name = "Hallmark"),
  list(coll = "M5", sub = "GO:BP",       name = "GO:BP"),
  list(coll = "M5", sub = "GO:CC",       name = "GO:CC"),
  list(coll = "M5", sub = "GO:MF",       name = "GO:MF"),
  list(coll = "M2", sub = "CP:REACTOME", name = "Reactome")
)

gene_sets <- list(); gene_set_source <- character(0)
for (cc in GSEA_COLLECTIONS) {
  args <- list(db_species = "MM", species = "Mus musculus",
               collection = cc$coll)
  if (!is.null(cc$sub)) args$subcollection <- cc$sub
  tbl <- do.call(msigdbr::msigdbr, args)
  stopifnot(nrow(tbl) > 0)
  gs  <- lapply(split(tbl$gene_symbol, tbl$gs_name), unique)
  # a set name appearing in two collections would otherwise be tested twice
  dup <- intersect(names(gs), names(gene_sets))
  if (length(dup))
    message("  [WARN] ", length(dup), " duplicate set names from ", cc$name,
            " dropped")
  gs <- gs[setdiff(names(gs), names(gene_sets))]
  message(sprintf("  %-10s %5d sets", cc$name, length(gs)))
  gene_sets       <- c(gene_sets, gs)
  gene_set_source <- c(gene_set_source,
                       setNames(rep(cc$name, length(gs)), names(gs)))
}
message("Gene sets total: ", length(gene_sets))
if (!length(gene_sets)) stop("No gene sets loaded; check collection names.")

.chk <- msigdbr::msigdbr(db_species = "MM", species = "Mus musculus",
                         collection = "MH")
message("db_version: ", .chk$db_version[1],
        "   (expect 2026.1.Mm; ortholog columns present: ",
        any(grepl("ortholog", names(.chk))), ")")

# =============================================================================
# MATRISOME MASTERLIST
# Loaded here so run_deg_gsea can hand it straight to plot_volcano.
# =============================================================================
matrisome_tbl <- load_matrisome()

dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
if (!exists("all_results")) all_results <- list()
#```

# 4. Run: compartment and cluster tests

#```{r DEG-GSEA-run}
assert_config_current()
if (!exists("gene_sets") || !exists("meta"))
  stop("Run the {r DEG-GSEA-data} chunk first.")

# Start from a clean slate. all_results persists for the whole R session, so a
# result computed under an older config chunk would otherwise survive here and
# break or silently contaminate the cross-test summaries. The global chunk
# appends to whatever this loop leaves behind.
if (exists("all_results") && length(all_results) > 0)
  message("Clearing ", length(all_results), " previous result(s): ",
          paste(names(all_results), collapse = ", "))
all_results <- list()

for (test_def in ALL_TESTS) {
  out_dir_test <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, test_def$subdir)
  dir.create(out_dir_test, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  result <- run_deg_gsea(
    seu       = seu,
    meta      = meta,
    test_def  = test_def,
    gene_sets = gene_sets,
    out_base  = out_dir_test,
    lfc_thr   = LFC_THRESHOLD,
    padj_thr  = PADJ_CUTOFF,
    min_cells = MIN_CELLS_PER_SAMPLE)

  if (!is.null(result))
    all_results[[test_def$label]] <- result
}

message("\n=== Cross-test DEG summary ===")
write_cross_test_summaries(all_results, OUTPUT_DIR)
message("\nAll outputs saved to: ", OUTPUT_DIR)
message("Done.")
#```

# 5. Run: global pooled test


#Safe to run on its own, provided chunks 2 and 3 have been run in this
#session.

#```{r DEG-GSEA-global}
assert_config_current()
if (!exists("gene_sets") || !exists("meta"))
  stop("Run the {r DEG-GSEA-data} chunk first.")
if (!exists("all_results")) all_results <- list()

message("\n", paste(rep("=", 60), collapse = ""))
message("GLOBAL Young vs Aged")
message(paste(rep("=", 60), collapse = ""))

.n_global <- sum(meta[["Compartments"]] %in% c("F", "CL", "S", "V"),
                 na.rm = TRUE)
message("Bins entering the global test: ", format(.n_global, big.mark = ","))
message("This subset is larger than any single compartment. If R runs out of ",
        "memory here,\nthe likely culprit is subset(seu, ...) rather than DESeq2.")

for (test_def in GLOBAL_TESTS) {
  out_dir_test <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, test_def$subdir)
  dir.create(out_dir_test, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  result <- run_deg_gsea(
    seu       = seu,
    meta      = meta,
    test_def  = test_def,
    gene_sets = gene_sets,
    out_base  = out_dir_test,
    lfc_thr   = LFC_THRESHOLD,
    padj_thr  = PADJ_CUTOFF,
    min_cells = MIN_CELLS_PER_SAMPLE)

  if (!is.null(result))
    all_results[[test_def$label]] <- result
}

# Rebuild the summaries. NOTE: if only this chunk was run in the session,
# all_results holds the global test alone and the two summary CSVs are
# OVERWRITTEN with global-only content. The message lists what went in.
message("\n=== Rebuilding cross-test summaries ===")
.summ <- write_cross_test_summaries(all_results, OUTPUT_DIR)
deg_summary  <- .summ$deg
gsea_summary <- .summ$gsea

# =============================================================================
# GLOBAL vs COMPARTMENT: what does pooling reveal, and what does it hide
# =============================================================================

GLOBAL_LABEL    <- "Global_AllCompartments"
COMPARTMENT_LBL <- c("Follicle", "CL", "Stroma", "Vascular")
.comp_present   <- intersect(COMPARTMENT_LBL, names(all_results))

if (GLOBAL_LABEL %in% names(all_results) && length(.comp_present) > 0) {

  g_deg <- deg_summary %>% filter(test == GLOBAL_LABEL)    %>% pull(gene) %>% unique()
  c_deg <- deg_summary %>% filter(test %in% .comp_present) %>% pull(gene) %>% unique()

  deg_cmp <- tibble(
    category = c("global only", "shared", "compartment only"),
    n_genes  = c(length(setdiff(g_deg, c_deg)),
                 length(intersect(g_deg, c_deg)),
                 length(setdiff(c_deg, g_deg))))

  message("\n--- DEGs: global vs compartment-stratified ---")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(deg_cmp)))
    message(sprintf("   %-18s %d", deg_cmp$category[i], deg_cmp$n_genes[i]))
  message("   'global only' genes are candidates for a COMPOSITIONAL shift:")
  message("   they emerge from pooling but are not significant within any")
  message("   single compartment.")

  g_gs <- gsea_summary %>% filter(test == GLOBAL_LABEL)    %>% pull(pathway) %>% unique()
  c_gs <- gsea_summary %>% filter(test %in% .comp_present) %>% pull(pathway) %>% unique()

  gsea_cmp <- tibble(
    category   = c("global only", "shared", "compartment only"),
    n_pathways = c(length(setdiff(g_gs, c_gs)),
                   length(intersect(g_gs, c_gs)),
                   length(setdiff(c_gs, g_gs))))

  message("\n--- GSEA pathways: global vs compartment-stratified ---")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(gsea_cmp)))
    message(sprintf("   %-18s %d", gsea_cmp$category[i], gsea_cmp$n_pathways[i]))

  deg_detail <- tibble(gene = union(g_deg, c_deg)) %>%
    mutate(in_global      = gene %in% g_deg,
           in_compartment = gene %in% c_deg,
           category = dplyr::case_when(
             in_global & !in_compartment ~ "global only",
             in_global &  in_compartment ~ "shared",
             TRUE                        ~ "compartment only")) %>%
    arrange(category, gene)
  write.csv(deg_detail,
            file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "DEG_global_vs_compartment.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  gsea_detail <- tibble(pathway = union(g_gs, c_gs)) %>%
    mutate(in_global      = pathway %in% g_gs,
           in_compartment = pathway %in% c_gs,
           category = dplyr::case_when(
             in_global & !in_compartment ~ "global only",
             in_global &  in_compartment ~ "shared",
             TRUE                        ~ "compartment only")) %>%
    arrange(category, pathway)
  write.csv(gsea_detail,
            file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "GSEA_global_vs_compartment.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  message("\nSaved: DEG_global_vs_compartment.csv")
  message("Saved: GSEA_global_vs_compartment.csv")

} else if (!GLOBAL_LABEL %in% names(all_results)) {
  message("\n[WARN] the global test produced no result, so the ",
          "global-vs-compartment comparison was skipped.")
} else {
  message("\n[WARN] no compartment tests in all_results, so the ",
          "global-vs-compartment comparison was skipped. Run ",
          "{r DEG-GSEA-run} in this session first if you want it.")
}

message("\nAll outputs saved to: ", OUTPUT_DIR)
message("Done.")
#```

# 6. Leading-edge redundancy


#Works on `all_results` in memory. Rewrites each `GSEA_*.csv` with the
#`leadingEdge` column that v4 dropped, writes one cluster table per test, and
#compares the top cluster's core genes across compartments.
#```{r GSEA-leading-edge-addon}
# ---- apply to everything already computed -----------------------------------
.subdirs <- c(vapply(ALL_TESTS,    function(t) t$subdir, character(1)),
              vapply(GLOBAL_TESTS, function(t) t$subdir, character(1)))
names(.subdirs) <- c(vapply(ALL_TESTS,    function(t) t$label, character(1)),
                     vapply(GLOBAL_TESTS, function(t) t$label, character(1)))

le_all <- list()
for (lbl in names(all_results)) {
  g <- all_results[[lbl]]$gsea
  if (is.null(g) || !"leadingEdge" %in% names(g)) next
  ob <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR,
                  if (lbl %in% names(.subdirs)) .subdirs[[lbl]] else ".")
  dir.create(ob, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  # rewrite the CSV, this time KEEPING the leading edge
  out <- as.data.frame(g)
  out$leadingEdge <- vapply(g$leadingEdge,
                            function(v) paste(v, collapse = "|"), character(1))
  write.csv(out, file.path(ob, paste0("GSEA_", lbl, "_Aged_vs_Young.csv")),
            row.names = FALSE)

  le_all[[lbl]] <- summarise_leading_edge(g, lbl, ob)
}

# ---- is the immune signal ONE finding or four? ------------------------------
comp <- intersect(c("Follicle", "CL", "Stroma", "Vascular"), names(le_all))
if (length(comp) >= 2) {
  tops <- lapply(comp, function(l) strsplit(le_all[[l]]$core_genes[1], "\\|")[[1]])
  names(tops) <- comp
  J <- outer(seq_along(comp), seq_along(comp), Vectorize(function(i, j) {
    a <- tops[[i]]; b <- tops[[j]]; u <- length(union(a, b))
    if (u == 0) NA_real_ else round(length(intersect(a, b)) / u, 3)
  }))
  dimnames(J) <- list(comp, comp)
  message("\nTop-cluster core-gene Jaccard between compartments:")
  print(J)
  write.csv(as.data.frame(J),
            file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "GSEA_topCluster_coreGene_overlap.csv"))
  off <- J[upper.tri(J)]
  message(sprintf("\nmedian off-diagonal overlap: %.2f", median(off, na.rm = TRUE)))
  if (median(off, na.rm = TRUE) >= 0.5)
    message("ONE shared signal across compartments, not four findings.") else
    message("Compartments differ; compartment-specific programmes are supported.")
}
#```

# 7. Meta-modules across tests

#```{r GSEA-meta-modules}
## =============================================================================
## META-MODULES: match leading-edge clusters across tests, name them by their
## genes rather than by their MSigDB label, and draw the summary figure.
##
## Answers two questions:
##   1. which programmes recur across compartments and cell types
##   2. which cluster labels are borrowed, i.e. the genes are a broad canonical
##      module wearing a specific-sounding name
##
## Requires in the session: le_all (from the leading-edge chunk), gene_sets,
## gene_set_source, OUTPUT_DIR, tidy_pathway, save_plot.
## =============================================================================

META_JACCARD      <- 0.40   # core-gene overlap to call two clusters the same module
META_MIN_CORE     <- 5      # ignore clusters with fewer core genes
HALLMARK_COVERAGE <- 0.50   # above this, the label is a broad canonical module

## ---- 1. flatten every cluster from every test into one table ---------------
le_tbl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(le_all), function(lbl) {
  x <- le_all[[lbl]]
  if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0) return(NULL)
  x$test <- lbl
  x
}))
le_tbl$core_list <- strsplit(le_tbl$core_genes, "\\|")
le_tbl <- le_tbl[vapply(le_tbl$core_list, length, integer(1)) >= META_MIN_CORE, ]
message("clusters carried forward: ", nrow(le_tbl), " from ",
        length(unique(le_tbl$test)), " tests")

## ---- 2. name each cluster by its genes, using Hallmark as the reference ----
## Hallmark is 50 curated, deliberately non-redundant sets. If a cluster's core
## genes sit largely inside one of them, that Hallmark set is the honest label
## whatever the GO or Reactome name says.
hallmark <- gene_sets[names(gene_sets) %in%
                        names(gene_set_source)[gene_set_source == "Hallmark"]]
