best_hallmark <- t(vapply(le_tbl$core_list, function(g) {
  cov <- vapply(hallmark, function(h) length(intersect(g, h)) / length(g), numeric(1))
  i <- which.max(cov)
  c(name = names(hallmark)[i], coverage = unname(cov[i]))
}, character(2)))
le_tbl$hallmark_match    <- best_hallmark[, "name"]
le_tbl$hallmark_coverage <- as.numeric(best_hallmark[, "coverage"])

## A cluster is flagged when a broad canonical programme explains most of its
## genes but the pathway name does not say so. Those are the borrowed labels.
.kw <- function(s) tolower(gsub("_", " ", sub("^HALLMARK_", "", s)))
le_tbl$label_supported <- mapply(function(rep_name, hm) {
  words <- setdiff(strsplit(.kw(hm), " ")[[1]], c("of","the","and","response","v1","v2"))
  any(vapply(words, function(w) grepl(w, tolower(rep_name), fixed = TRUE), logical(1)))
}, le_tbl$representative, le_tbl$hallmark_match)
le_tbl$borrowed_label <- le_tbl$hallmark_coverage >= HALLMARK_COVERAGE &
                         !le_tbl$label_supported

message("clusters whose genes are >= ", HALLMARK_COVERAGE * 100,
        "% explained by one Hallmark set: ",
        sum(le_tbl$hallmark_coverage >= HALLMARK_COVERAGE))
message("  of which the pathway name does NOT reflect it (borrowed label): ",
        sum(le_tbl$borrowed_label))

## ---- 3. group clusters into meta-modules by core-gene overlap -------------
ord <- order(le_tbl$rep_padj)
le_tbl <- le_tbl[ord, ]
n <- nrow(le_tbl); mm <- rep(NA_integer_, n); k <- 0L
for (i in seq_len(n)) {
  if (!is.na(mm[i])) next
  k <- k + 1L; mm[i] <- k
  if (i < n) for (j in (i + 1):n) {
    if (!is.na(mm[j])) next
    a <- le_tbl$core_list[[i]]; b <- le_tbl$core_list[[j]]
    u <- length(union(a, b))
    if (u > 0 && length(intersect(a, b)) / u >= META_JACCARD) mm[j] <- k
  }
}
le_tbl$meta_module <- mm
message("meta-modules: ", k, " across ", nrow(le_tbl), " clusters")

## ---- 4. one row per meta-module ------------------------------------------
meta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(k), function(m) {
  idx <- which(le_tbl$meta_module == m)
  g   <- table(unlist(le_tbl$core_list[idx]))
  core <- names(g)[g >= max(1, ceiling(length(idx) / 2))]
  hm  <- names(sort(table(le_tbl$hallmark_match[idx]), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
  data.frame(
    meta_module      = m,
    n_tests          = length(unique(le_tbl$test[idx])),
    tests            = paste(sort(unique(le_tbl$test[idx])), collapse = "|"),
    n_clusters       = length(idx),
    n_pathways_total = sum(le_tbl$n_pathways[idx]),
    representative   = le_tbl$representative[idx[1]],
    hallmark_match   = hm,
    mean_hallmark_cov = round(mean(le_tbl$hallmark_coverage[idx]), 3),
    any_borrowed     = any(le_tbl$borrowed_label[idx]),
    direction        = if (mean(le_tbl$rep_NES[idx]) > 0) "Up in Aged" else "Up in Young",
    mean_NES         = round(mean(le_tbl$rep_NES[idx]), 3),
    n_core_genes     = length(core),
    core_genes       = paste(head(core, 60), collapse = "|"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
meta <- meta[order(-meta$n_tests, -meta$n_pathways_total), ]

write.csv(le_tbl[, setdiff(names(le_tbl), "core_list")],
          file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "GSEA_clusters_annotated_all_tests.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(meta, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "GSEA_meta_modules.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

message("\nmeta-modules present in >= 3 tests:")
top <- meta[meta$n_tests >= 3, ]
for (i in seq_len(min(nrow(top), 12)))
  message(sprintf("  %2d tests | %4d pathways | %-34s | %s | cov %.2f%s",
                  top$n_tests[i], top$n_pathways_total[i],
                  substr(tidy_pathway(top$representative[i], 34), 1, 34),
                  top$direction[i], top$mean_hallmark_cov[i],
                  ifelse(top$any_borrowed[i], "  [label borrowed]", "")))

## ---- 5. the figure: meta-module x test ------------------------------------
MM_MIN_TESTS <- 3
MM_MAX_ROWS  <- 25

sel <- meta$meta_module[meta$n_tests >= MM_MIN_TESTS][seq_len(
  min(MM_MAX_ROWS, sum(meta$n_tests >= MM_MIN_TESTS)))]

plot_df <- le_tbl[le_tbl$meta_module %in% sel, ]
lab <- setNames(
  ifelse(meta$any_borrowed[match(sel, meta$meta_module)],
         paste0(tidy_pathway(meta$hallmark_match[match(sel, meta$meta_module)], 40),
                " *"),
         tidy_pathway(meta$representative[match(sel, meta$meta_module)], 40)),
  sel)
plot_df$module_label <- lab[as.character(plot_df$meta_module)]
plot_df$module_label <- factor(
  plot_df$module_label,
  levels = rev(unique(lab[as.character(sel)])))

test_order <- c("Global_AllCompartments", "Follicle", "CL", "Stroma", "Vascular",
                setdiff(unique(plot_df$test),
                        c("Global_AllCompartments","Follicle","CL","Stroma","Vascular")))
plot_df$test <- factor(plot_df$test, levels = intersect(test_order, unique(plot_df$test)))

p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = test, y = module_label)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_pathways, fill = rep_NES),
             shape = 21, colour = "grey25", stroke = 0.25) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#007A7A", mid = "white", high = "#B57BEE",
                       midpoint = 0, name = "NES") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 7), name = "pathway names\ncollapsed") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = "* label taken from the best-matching Hallmark set; the pathway name did not reflect its genes") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 5.5, colour = "grey35", hjust = 0),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey94", linewidth = 0.2),
        legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.35, "cm"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6.5))

save_plot(p, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "GSEA_meta_modules_across_tests"),
          width = 7.5, height = max(3.5, 0.26 * length(sel) + 2))
message("\nwrote GSEA_meta_modules_across_tests")

#```

# 8. Over-representation analysis on the DEG list


#GSEA above uses the full ranked gene list and therefore ignores
#`LFC_THRESHOLD` entirely. If you want an enrichment test that *does* respect
#your cut, that is over-representation analysis (ORA): take the genes passing
#padj < `PADJ_CUTOFF` and |LFC| > `LFC_THRESHOLD`, and ask whether each gene set
#contains more of them than chance, against a universe of the genes actually
#tested. It answers a different question from GSEA and the two often disagree,
#which is informative rather than a problem.

#Up and down are run separately, because pooling them lets a set enriched for
#both directions look significant with no coherent direction.

#Uses `fgsea::fora()`. Verify the signature with `?fora` on your installed
#version before trusting the output; the chunk stops if the function is absent.

#```{r ORA-from-DEG, eval=FALSE}
assert_config_current()
if (!"fora" %in% getNamespaceExports("fgsea"))
  stop("fgsea::fora() not available in fgsea ", packageVersion("fgsea"),
       ". Update fgsea, or use clusterProfiler::enricher instead.")
if (!exists("gene_sets"))
  stop("Run the {r DEG-GSEA-data} chunk first, gene_sets is needed.")

ora_dir <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "4_ORA")
dir.create(ora_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

deg_files <- list.files(OUTPUT_DIR, pattern = "^DEG_.*_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$",
                        recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)

ora_all <- bind_rows(lapply(deg_files, function(f) {
  d   <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  lbl <- sub("^DEG_(.*)_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$", "\\1", basename(f))
  if (!"log2FoldChange_mle" %in% names(d) || "padj_lfcthr" %in% names(d)) {
    message("[STALE, SKIPPED] ", basename(f)); return(NULL)
  }
  d$lfc_call <- d[[DEG_LFC_COL]]

  # The universe is the genes that entered the test, NOT all annotated genes.
  # Using the whole genome as the universe inflates significance.
  universe <- d$gene[!is.na(d$padj)]
  sig <- d %>% filter(!is.na(padj), padj < PADJ_CUTOFF,
                      abs(lfc_call) >= LFC_THRESHOLD)

  bind_rows(lapply(c("Up_Aged", "Up_Young"), function(dir_lbl) {
    genes <- if (dir_lbl == "Up_Aged")
      sig$gene[sig$lfc_call > 0] else sig$gene[sig$lfc_call < 0]
    message(lbl, " / ", dir_lbl, ": ", length(genes), " genes of ",
            length(universe), " tested")
    if (length(genes) < 5) {
      message("  too few genes, skipped")
      return(NULL)
    }
    res <- fgsea::fora(pathways = gene_sets, genes = genes,
                       universe = universe, minSize = 10, maxSize = 500)
    as.data.frame(res) %>%
      mutate(test = lbl, direction = dir_lbl,
             n_query = length(genes), n_universe = length(universe),
             gene_ratio = overlap / size,
             collection = unname(gene_set_source[pathway]))
  }))
}))

ora_out <- ora_all
ora_out$overlapGenes <- vapply(ora_all$overlapGenes,
                               function(v) paste(v, collapse = "|"), character(1))
write.csv(ora_out, file.path(ora_dir, "ORA_all_tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
message("ORA rows written: ", nrow(ora_all),
        "  significant at padj < 0.05: ",
        sum(ora_all$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE))

# one dot plot per test, both directions on the same panel
for (lbl in unique(ora_all$test)) {
  sig <- ora_all %>% filter(test == lbl, !is.na(padj), padj < 0.05)
  if (nrow(sig) == 0) {
    message(lbl, ": no ORA hits at padj < 0.05"); next
  }

  shim <- sig
  shim$leadingEdge <- sig$overlapGenes
  shim$NES <- ifelse(sig$direction == "Up_Aged", sig$gene_ratio, -sig$gene_ratio)
  cl <- summarise_leading_edge(shim, paste0("ORA_", lbl), ora_dir)
  if (is.null(cl)) { message(lbl, ": no clusters"); next }

  keep <- cl %>% group_by(direction) %>%
    slice_max(n_pathways, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>% pull(representative)
  df <- sig %>% filter(pathway %in% keep)
  if (nrow(df) == 0) { message(lbl, ": nothing to plot"); next }

  df <- df %>%
    mutate(pathway_label  = tidy_pathway(pathway),
           neg_log10_padj = -log10(padj)) %>%
    arrange(direction, gene_ratio)
  df$pathway_label <- make.unique(df$pathway_label, sep = " ")
  df$pathway_label <- factor(df$pathway_label, levels = df$pathway_label)

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = gene_ratio, y = pathway_label)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = gene_ratio,
                     y = pathway_label, yend = pathway_label),
                 colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_point(aes(size = overlap, colour = neg_log10_padj)) +
    facet_grid(direction ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "C", direction = -1, end = 0.9,
                           name = expression(-log[10]~italic(p)[adj])) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 6), name = "DEGs in set") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .06))) +
    labs(title = paste0(lbl, ": ORA on DEGs (padj < ", PADJ_CUTOFF,
                        ", |LFC| > ", LFC_THRESHOLD, ")"),
         x = "Gene ratio (DEGs in set / set size)", y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
    theme(plot.title  = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 9),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
          strip.text  = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
          legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.35, "cm"))

  save_plot(p, file.path(ora_dir, paste0("ORA_dotplot_", lbl)),
            width  = GSEA_DOT_W,
            height = max(3.4, 0.24 * nrow(df) + 2.0))
}
message("ORA written to: ", ora_dir)
#```

# 9. Curation step 1: build the QC template

#Reads every per-test GSEA / ORA result, stamps the leading-edge cluster
#assignment onto each pathway row, and writes one editable template per test as
#`<original>_toplot.csv`. Nothing is filtered away: every significant pathway is
#present, with a pre-filled `plot` column you overwrite by hand.

#Three hard filters are applied before writing, in this order: `padj <
#CURATE_PADJ`, `size <= CURATE_MAX_SIZE`, and `independent == TRUE`. Rows failing
#any of them never reach the template. None of this changes a p-value: the tested
#family is fixed, these are presentation decisions applied downstream.

#`is_rep` is then **recomputed** over the survivors, because
#`summarise_leading_edge()` chose each cluster's representative before the size
#filter existed and that representative may have just been dropped. The pre-fill
#is a suggestion, not a decision: `plot` starts as "plot" on one row per
#surviving cluster (the lowest-padj member) and "no" everywhere else.

#Existing `_toplot.csv` files are never overwritten unless
#`CURATE_OVERWRITE <- TRUE`, so re-running this chunk cannot destroy manual work.

#```{r curation-template, eval=FALSE}
assert_config_current()

CURATE_DIR      <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "5_Curation")
CURATE_OVERWRITE <- TRUE   # TRUE wipes your manual edits; leave FALSE

# Only rows at or below this adjusted p-value enter the curation template.
# Kept separate from PADJ_CUTOFF (which is the DEG gene-level cut) so the two
# can be reported independently in the methods.
CURATE_PADJ <- 0.05

# Hard drops applied BEFORE the template is written. These are curation
# decisions, not analysis decisions: the tested family is unchanged, so no padj
# moves. Report both numbers in the methods.
CURATE_MAX_SIZE    <- 200    # drop gene sets larger than this
CURATE_INDEP_ONLY  <- TRUE   # drop sets collapsePathways flagged as redundant

dir.create(CURATE_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# ---- stamp le_cluster / is_rep from the cluster summary onto pathway rows ----
stamp_clusters <- function(df, cluster_csv) {
  df$le_cluster      <- NA_integer_
  df$cluster_size    <- NA_integer_
  df$is_rep          <- NA
  df$cluster_members <- NA_character_
  if (is.null(cluster_csv) || !file.exists(cluster_csv)) {
    message("  [WARN] cluster file absent: ", basename(as.character(cluster_csv)),
            " - le_cluster left NA")
    return(df)
  }
  cl <- read.csv(cluster_csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(cl))) {
    mem <- strsplit(cl$member_pathways[i], "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    j   <- which(df$pathway %in% mem)
    if (!length(j)) next
    df$le_cluster[j]      <- cl$le_cluster[i]
    df$cluster_size[j]    <- cl$n_pathways[i]
    df$is_rep[j]          <- df$pathway[j] == cl$representative[i]
    df$cluster_members[j] <- cl$member_pathways[i]
  }
  df
}

# ---- hard curation filters ---------------------------------------------------
# NOTE ON ORDER: summarise_leading_edge() picked each cluster's representative
# from ALL significant pathways, before these filters existed. A representative
# can therefore be dropped here, leaving its cluster with no is_rep row. So
# is_rep is RECOMPUTED below over the surviving rows only.
apply_curation_filters <- function(df) {
  n0 <- nrow(df)

  if ("size" %in% names(df)) {
    n1 <- nrow(df)
    df <- df[!is.na(df$size) & df$size <= CURATE_MAX_SIZE, , drop = FALSE]
    message("    size > ", CURATE_MAX_SIZE, ": dropped ", n1 - nrow(df))
  } else {
    message("    [WARN] no 'size' column; size filter not applied")
  }

  if (CURATE_INDEP_ONLY && "independent" %in% names(df)) {
    if (all(is.na(df$independent))) {
      message("    [WARN] 'independent' is all NA (collapsePathways did not ",
              "run); redundancy filter NOT applied")
    } else {
      n1 <- nrow(df)
      df <- df[df$independent %in% TRUE, , drop = FALSE]
      message("    independent != TRUE: dropped ", n1 - nrow(df))
    }
  }
  if (!nrow(df)) { message("    nothing survived the filters"); return(df) }

  # re-designate the lowest-padj SURVIVING member of each cluster. Direction is
  # part of the key because an ORA term can be significant in both directions
  # while carrying a single le_cluster.
  key <- if ("direction" %in% names(df))
    paste(df$le_cluster, df$direction) else as.character(df$le_cluster)
  key[is.na(df$le_cluster)] <- paste0("_unclustered_", which(is.na(df$le_cluster)))

  df$n_kept_in_cluster <- NA_integer_
  df$is_rep <- FALSE
  for (k in unique(key)) {
    j <- which(key == k)
    df$n_kept_in_cluster[j] <- length(j)
    df$is_rep[j[which.min(df$padj[j])]] <- TRUE
  }
  message("    kept ", nrow(df), " of ", n0, " rows in ",
          length(unique(key)), " leading-edge clusters")
  df
}

# ---- column order that makes hand-editing in Excel bearable ------------------
front_cols <- function(df) {
  first <- c("plot", "display_label", "notes", "pathway", "le_cluster",
             "cluster_size", "n_kept_in_cluster", "is_rep", "independent",
             "size", "NES", "foldEnrichment", "gene_ratio", "overlap",
             "padj", "pval", "direction", "collection", "test")
  first <- first[first %in% names(df)]
  rest  <- setdiff(names(df), c(first, "leadingEdge", "overlapGenes",
                                "cluster_members"))
  tail  <- intersect(c("cluster_members", "leadingEdge", "overlapGenes"),
                     names(df))
  df[, c(first, rest, tail), drop = FALSE]
}

write_template <- function(df, out_name) {
  out <- file.path(CURATE_DIR, out_name)
  if (file.exists(out) && !CURATE_OVERWRITE) {
    message("  [KEPT] ", out_name, " already exists, not overwritten")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  # foldEnrichment = (overlap/n_query)/(size/n_universe), i.e. observed over
  # expected, and it supersedes our home-made gene_ratio = overlap/size. Keeping
  # both invites reporting the wrong one, so gene_ratio is dropped when
  # foldEnrichment is available.
  if (all(c("foldEnrichment", "gene_ratio") %in% names(df))) {
    df$gene_ratio <- NULL
    message("    gene_ratio dropped; foldEnrichment is the effect size")
  }
  df$display_label <- tidy_pathway(df$pathway)
  df$notes         <- ""
  # size and independence are already enforced by apply_curation_filters(), so
  # the only remaining pre-fill rule is one row per surviving cluster.
  df$plot <- ifelse(!is.na(df$is_rep) & df$is_rep, "plot", "no")
  ord <- order(is.na(df$le_cluster), df$le_cluster, df$padj)
  df  <- front_cols(df[ord, , drop = FALSE])
  write.csv(df, out, row.names = FALSE)
  message("  [WRITTEN] ", out_name, ": ", nrow(df), " rows, ",
          sum(df$plot == "plot"), " pre-marked 'plot'")
}

# ---- GSEA --------------------------------------------------------------------
gsea_files <- list.files(OUTPUT_DIR, pattern = "^GSEA_.*_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$",
                         recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
message("GSEA result files found: ", length(gsea_files))
for (f in gsea_files) {
  lbl <- sub("^GSEA_(.*)_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$", "\\1", basename(f))
  d0  <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  d   <- d0[!is.na(d0$padj) & d0$padj < CURATE_PADJ, , drop = FALSE]
  message(lbl, ": ", nrow(d), " of ", nrow(d0),
          " tested sets kept at padj < ", CURATE_PADJ,
          " (", nrow(d0) - nrow(d), " dropped)")
  if (!nrow(d)) next
  d <- stamp_clusters(d, file.path(dirname(f),
                                   paste0("GSEA_leadingEdge_clusters_", lbl, ".csv")))
  d <- apply_curation_filters(d)
  if (!nrow(d)) next
  write_template(d, sub("\\.csv$", "_toplot.csv", basename(f)))
}

# ---- ORA ---------------------------------------------------------------------
ora_file <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "4_ORA", "ORA_all_tests.csv")
if (file.exists(ora_file)) {
  ora <- read.csv(ora_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (lbl in unique(ora$test)) {
    d0 <- ora[ora$test == lbl, , drop = FALSE]
    d  <- d0[!is.na(d0$padj) & d0$padj < CURATE_PADJ, , drop = FALSE]
    message("ORA ", lbl, ": ", nrow(d), " of ", nrow(d0),
            " terms kept at padj < ", CURATE_PADJ,
            " (", nrow(d0) - nrow(d), " dropped)")
    if (!nrow(d)) next
    d <- stamp_clusters(d, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "4_ORA",
                                     paste0("GSEA_leadingEdge_clusters_ORA_",
                                            lbl, ".csv")))
    # a term can be significant in BOTH directions; the cluster file carries no
    # direction, so both rows inherit the same le_cluster. apply_curation_filters
    # keys on cluster + direction so the two are not collapsed into one.
    # ORA has no 'independent' column, so only the size filter applies here.
    d <- apply_curation_filters(d)
    if (!nrow(d)) next
    write_template(d, paste0("ORA_", lbl, "_toplot.csv"))
  }
} else {
  message("ORA_all_tests.csv not found; ORA templates skipped")
}
message("Templates written to: ", CURATE_DIR)
```

# 10. Curation step 2: manuscript dot plots from the curated list


Plots only the rows you marked. Finds every `*_toplot.csv` anywhere under
`OUTPUT_DIR`, so it does not matter which folder you edit them in.

Required columns: `pathway`, `plot`. Optional: `display_label` (the name printed
on the axis; falls back to the tidied pathway name if blank), `panel` (adds a
facet). Accepted "yes" values in `plot`, case-insensitive: plot, yes, y, true, 1.
Anything else is treated as "no" and reported.

The file type is detected from its columns: `NES` present means GSEA (x = NES,
reference line at 0), otherwise `foldEnrichment` means ORA (x = fold enrichment,
reference line at 1, faceted by direction). `gene_ratio` is used only as a
fallback for older ORA files that lack `foldEnrichment`.

```{r manuscript-dotplots, eval=FALSE}
assert_config_current()

MANU_DIR <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "6_Manuscript")
dir.create(MANU_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
MANU_DOT_W <- 7.5
MANU_DOT_TOP_PER_DIR <- 15
MANU_DOT_H_MAX       <- 12

is_marked <- function(x)
  tolower(trimws(as.character(x))) %in% c("plot", "yes", "y", "true", "1")

curated <- list.files(OUTPUT_DIR, pattern = "_toplot\\.csv$",
                      recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
if (!length(curated))
  stop("No *_toplot.csv found under ", OUTPUT_DIR,
       ". Run the {r curation-template} chunk first.")
message("Curated files found: ", length(curated))

for (f in curated) {
  lbl <- sub("_toplot$", "", tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f)))
  d   <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  miss <- setdiff(c("pathway", "plot"), names(d))
  if (length(miss)) {
    message("[SKIP] ", basename(f), ": missing column(s) ",
            paste(miss, collapse = ", ")); next
  }
  vals <- unique(tolower(trimws(as.character(d$plot))))
  bad  <- setdiff(vals, c("plot","yes","y","true","1","no","n","false","0",""))
  if (length(bad))
    message("[WARN] ", basename(f), ": unrecognised plot values treated as ",
            "'no': ", paste(bad, collapse = ", "))

  d <- d[is_marked(d$plot), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) { message("[SKIP] ", basename(f), ": nothing marked"); next }

  mode <- NA_character_
  if ("NES" %in% names(d)) mode <- "GSEA"
  else if (any(c("foldEnrichment", "gene_ratio") %in% names(d))) mode <- "ORA"
  if (is.na(mode)) {
    message("[SKIP] ", basename(f),
            ": none of NES / foldEnrichment / gene_ratio present"); next
  }

  # axis labels: display_label if supplied and non-blank, else tidied pathway
  lab <- tidy_pathway(d$pathway)
  if ("display_label" %in% names(d)) {
    dl  <- trimws(as.character(d$display_label))
    lab <- ifelse(!is.na(dl) & nzchar(dl), dl, lab)
  }
  d$pathway_label <- lab

  # padj == 0 underflows to Inf on the -log10 scale; draw at the panel maximum
  d$neg_log10_padj <- -log10(d$padj)
  fin <- is.finite(d$neg_log10_padj)
  if (any(!fin)) {
    ceil <- if (any(fin)) max(d$neg_log10_padj[fin]) else 300
    message("  ", sum(!fin), " pathway(s) with padj = 0 drawn at ",
            round(ceil, 1), " on the colour scale")
    d$neg_log10_padj[!fin] <- ceil
  }

  if (mode == "GSEA") {
    ok   <- which(!is.na(d$NES))
    pos  <- ok[d$NES[ok] >  0]
    neg  <- ok[d$NES[ok] <= 0]
    pos  <- pos[order(-d$NES[pos])]
    neg  <- neg[order( d$NES[neg])]
    keep <- sort(c(head(pos, MANU_DOT_TOP_PER_DIR),
                   head(neg, MANU_DOT_TOP_PER_DIR)))
  } else {
    eff  <- if ("foldEnrichment" %in% names(d)) d$foldEnrichment else d$gene_ratio
    keep <- sort(order(-eff, d$padj)[seq_len(min(nrow(d),
                                                 2 * MANU_DOT_TOP_PER_DIR))])
  }
  if (length(keep) < nrow(d))
    message("[CAPPED] ", basename(f), ": ", nrow(d),
            " rows marked 'plot'; plotting ", length(keep),
            if (mode == "GSEA") " (top/bottom NES)" else
              " (top by effect size)")
  d <- d[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  if (mode == "GSEA") {
    d <- d[order(d$NES), , drop = FALSE]
    d$pathway_label <- make.unique(d$pathway_label, sep = " ")
    d$pathway_label <- factor(d$pathway_label, levels = d$pathway_label)
    x_abs <- max(abs(d$NES), na.rm = TRUE)

    p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = NES, y = pathway_label)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
                 colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.25) +
      geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = NES,
                       y = pathway_label, yend = pathway_label),
                   colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.25) +
      geom_point(aes(size = size, fill = neg_log10_padj),
                 shape = 21, colour = "black", stroke = 0.25) +
      scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 6), name = "Genes in set") +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-x_abs, x_abs) * 1.08,
                         expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
      labs(x = "Normalised Enrichment Score (NES)", y = NULL)
  } else {
    if (!"direction" %in% names(d)) d$direction <- "All"

    # foldEnrichment is observed/expected, so its null value is 1, not 0. The
    # lollipop baseline and the reference line both sit at 1. gene_ratio is a
    # fraction with a null at 0, so the baseline moves accordingly.
    if ("foldEnrichment" %in% names(d)) {
      x_var <- "foldEnrichment"; x_null <- 1
      x_lab <- "Fold enrichment (observed / expected)"
    } else {
      x_var <- "gene_ratio"; x_null <- 0
      x_lab <- "Gene ratio (DEGs in set / set size)"
    }
    d <- d[order(d$direction, d[[x_var]]), , drop = FALSE]
    d$pathway_label <- make.unique(d$pathway_label, sep = " ")
    d$pathway_label <- factor(d$pathway_label, levels = d$pathway_label)
    size_var <- if ("overlap" %in% names(d)) "overlap" else "size"
    x_lo <- min(x_null, min(d[[x_var]], na.rm = TRUE))

    p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = .data[[x_var]], y = pathway_label)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = x_null, linetype = "dashed",
                 colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.25) +
      geom_segment(aes(x = x_null, xend = .data[[x_var]],
                       y = pathway_label, yend = pathway_label),
                   colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.25) +
      geom_point(aes(size = .data[[size_var]], fill = neg_log10_padj),
                 shape = 21, colour = "black", stroke = 0.25) +
      facet_grid(direction ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
      scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 7.5), name = "DEGs in set") +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(x_lo, NA),
                         expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .06))) +
      labs(x = x_lab, y = NULL)
  }

  if ("panel" %in% names(d) && length(unique(d$panel)) > 1)
    p <- p + facet_grid(panel ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y")

  p <- p +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C", direction = 1, begin = 0.05, end = 1,
                         name = expression(-log[10]~italic(p)[adj])) +
    guides(size = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21,
                                                   fill = "grey70",
                                                   colour = "black"))) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
          strip.text  = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
          legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.text  = element_text(size = 7),
          legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.35, "cm"),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey93",
                                            linewidth = 0.2))

  save_plot(p, file.path(MANU_DIR, paste0("Curated_dotplot_", lbl)),
            width  = MANU_DOT_W,
            height = min(MANU_DOT_H_MAX, max(3.2, 0.24 * nrow(d) + 1.7)))

  # the exact rows behind the figure, for the figure legend and the record
  write.csv(d[, setdiff(names(d), c("leadingEdge", "overlapGenes",
                                    "cluster_members")), drop = FALSE],
            file.path(MANU_DIR, paste0("Curated_dotplot_", lbl, "_source.csv")),
            row.names = FALSE)
  message("[PLOTTED] ", lbl, ": ", nrow(d), " pathways (", mode, ")")
}
message("Manuscript dot plots written to: ", MANU_DIR)
#```

# 11. Matrisome by category, and the ligand-receptor scatter

## Matrisome regulation by category

#x is the percentage of **detected** genes in each category that are DEGs, so the
#six categories are comparable despite ranging from 36 to 367 annotated members.
#Detection coverage sits in the y-axis label as `Collagens (38/44)`, meaning
#detected out of annotated. Bars are dodged, both directions on the right, with
#`n (x%)` at each bar end.

#"Detected" means present in the DEG table with a non-`NA` `padj`. Genes dropped
#by the pseudobulk count filter, or given `padj = NA` by DESeq2's independent
#filtering, were never tested and are excluded from the denominator.

#Both panels resized for a narrow, stacked layout. Paste at the end of the Rmd and
#run Panel A first.

#*Sizing.** 1 inch = 25.4 mm. The defaults below are `3.0 x 1.7 in` (76 x 43 mm)
#for Panel A and `3.0 x 2.0 in` (76 x 51 mm) for Panel B, so the pair stacks into
#roughly 76 x 94 mm. Change `MBAR_W/MBAR_H` and `LR_W/LR_H` to match your real
#slot; everything else scales from them.

---

## Panel A: matrisome regulation by category

#Thinner bars, no gap between the two bars of a category, legend inside the plot
#area at top right. Move the legend by editing the two numbers in
#`leg_inside(0.99, 0.99, ...)`; `leg_inside(0.99, 0.02, just = c(1, 0))` puts it
#bottom right instead.

#```{r matrisome-category-bar, eval=FALSE}
assert_config_current()

MBAR_TEST <- "Global_AllCompartments"
MBAR_DIR  <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "6_Manuscript")
MBAR_REF_DIR <- "Z:/Visium_Data/001_SpatialX"
MBAR_W <- 3.0        # inches -> 76 mm
MBAR_H <- 1.7        # inches -> 43 mm
MBAR_BAR_W <- 0.85   # bar thickness AND dodge width; equal = bars touch
MBAR_MIN_TESTED <- 15

MBAR_ORDER <- c("Collagens", "ECM Glycoproteins", "Proteoglycans",
                "ECM Regulators", "ECM-affiliated Proteins", "Secreted Factors")

VOLC_COLS <- c("Up in Aged"  = "#B57BEE",
               "Up in Young" = "#007A7A",
               "NS"          = "grey70")

# ggplot2 3.5.0 replaced numeric legend.position with legend.position.inside
leg_inside <- function(x, y, just = c(x, y)) {
  if (utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "3.5.0")
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "inside",
                   legend.position.inside = c(x, y),
                   legend.justification = just)
  else
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = c(x, y),
                   legend.justification = just)
}

dir.create(MBAR_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# ---- matrisome table: reuse the volcano chunk's object, or load it ----------
if (!exists("matri")) {
  mfile <- list.files(MBAR_REF_DIR,
                      pattern = "^Mm_Matrisome_Masterlist.*\\.csv$",
                      full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(mfile)) stop("Matrisome CSV not found in ", MBAR_REF_DIR)
  rawm <- read.csv(mfile[1], stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  nm   <- gsub("[^a-z]", "", tolower(names(rawm)))
  need <- c("genesymbol", "matrisomedivision", "matrisomecategory")
  miss <- need[!need %in% nm]
  if (length(miss))
    stop("Matrisome CSV missing column(s) for: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "),
         ". Columns present: ", paste(names(rawm), collapse = ", "))
  matri <- data.frame(
    gene               = trimws(as.character(rawm[[which(nm == "genesymbol")[1]]])),
    matrisome_division = as.character(rawm[[which(nm == "matrisomedivision")[1]]]),
    matrisome_category = as.character(rawm[[which(nm == "matrisomecategory")[1]]]),
    stringsAsFactors   = FALSE)
  matri <- matri[nzchar(matri$gene) & !is.na(matri$gene), , drop = FALSE]
  matri <- matri[!duplicated(matri$gene), , drop = FALSE]
}
n_annot <- table(matri$matrisome_category)
message("Matrisome masterlist: ", nrow(matri), " symbols")

# ---- the DEG table ----------------------------------------------------------
f <- list.files(OUTPUT_DIR,
                pattern = paste0("^DEG_", MBAR_TEST, "_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$"),
                recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
if (!length(f)) stop("No DEG file for ", MBAR_TEST)
d <- read.csv(f[1], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d$lfc <- d[[DEG_LFC_COL]]
d <- d[!is.na(d$padj) & !is.na(d$lfc), , drop = FALSE]
message("Genes tested in ", MBAR_TEST, ": ", nrow(d))

d <- merge(d, matri, by = "gene")
message("  of which matrisome: ", nrow(d))

d$sig <- dplyr::case_when(
  d$padj < PADJ_CUTOFF & d$lfc >=  LFC_THRESHOLD ~ "Up in Aged",
  d$padj < PADJ_CUTOFF & d$lfc <= -LFC_THRESHOLD ~ "Up in Young",
  TRUE                                           ~ "NS")

# ---- per-category table -----------------------------------------------------
cats  <- intersect(MBAR_ORDER, unique(d$matrisome_category))
extra <- setdiff(unique(d$matrisome_category), MBAR_ORDER)
if (length(extra)) {
  message("[WARN] category not in MBAR_ORDER, appended: ",
          paste(extra, collapse = ", "))
  cats <- c(cats, extra)
}

tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cats, function(cc) {
  s <- d[d$matrisome_category == cc, , drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(category    = cc,
             division    = s$matrisome_division[1],
             n_annotated = as.integer(n_annot[cc]),
             n_detected  = nrow(s),
             n_up_aged   = sum(s$sig == "Up in Aged"),
             n_up_young  = sum(s$sig == "Up in Young"),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
tab$pct_detected <- 100 * tab$n_detected / tab$n_annotated
tab$pct_up_aged  <- 100 * tab$n_up_aged  / tab$n_detected
tab$pct_up_young <- 100 * tab$n_up_young / tab$n_detected
print(tab, row.names = FALSE)

thin <- tab$category[tab$n_detected < MBAR_MIN_TESTED]
if (length(thin))
  message("[WARN] fewer than ", MBAR_MIN_TESTED, " genes detected in: ",
          paste(thin, collapse = ", "),
          " - one gene moves the percentage a long way")

write.csv(tab, file.path(MBAR_DIR,
          paste0("Matrisome_category_counts_", MBAR_TEST, ".csv")),
          row.names = FALSE)

# ---- long form --------------------------------------------------------------
tab$cat_lab <- paste0(tab$category, " (", tab$n_detected, "/",
                      tab$n_annotated, ")")
plt <- rbind(
  data.frame(cat_lab = tab$cat_lab, sig = "Up in Young",
             n = tab$n_up_young, pct = tab$pct_up_young,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  data.frame(cat_lab = tab$cat_lab, sig = "Up in Aged",
             n = tab$n_up_aged,  pct = tab$pct_up_aged,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
plt$cat_lab <- factor(plt$cat_lab, levels = rev(tab$cat_lab))
plt$sig     <- factor(plt$sig, levels = c("Up in Young", "Up in Aged"))
plt$lab     <- paste0(plt$n, " (", round(plt$pct), "%)")

x_max <- max(plt$pct, na.rm = TRUE)
if (x_max == 0) stop("No matrisome DEGs in ", MBAR_TEST, "; nothing to plot.")

# equal col width and dodge width = the two bars of a category touch
pos <- position_dodge(width = MBAR_BAR_W)

p <- ggplot(plt, aes(x = pct, y = cat_lab, fill = sig)) +
  geom_col(position = pos, width = MBAR_BAR_W,
           colour = "black", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab), position = pos,
            hjust = -0.12, size = 1.9, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = VOLC_COLS, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, x_max * 1.55),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  labs(x = "% of detected genes in category", y = NULL) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.y       = element_text(size = 6),
        axis.text.x       = element_text(size = 6),
        axis.title.x      = element_text(size = 6.5),
        axis.ticks        = element_line(linewidth = 0.2),
        legend.direction  = "vertical",
        legend.text       = element_text(size = 5.8),
        legend.key.size   = grid::unit(0.22, "cm"),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.75),
                                         colour = NA),
        legend.margin     = margin(1, 2, 1, 2),
        plot.margin       = margin(3, 6, 3, 3)) +
  leg_inside(0.99, 0.99)

save_plot(p, file.path(MBAR_DIR,
          paste0("Matrisome_category_bar_", MBAR_TEST)),
          width = MBAR_W, height = MBAR_H)
message("Matrisome category bar written to: ", MBAR_DIR)
#```

## Ligand-receptor coordination scatter, ConnectomeDB2025

#```{r lr-scatter-connectomedb, eval=FALSE}
#assert_config_current()

LR_TEST    <- "Global_AllCompartments"
LR_DIR     <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "6_Manuscript")
LR_REF_DIR <- "Z:/Visium_Data/001_SpatialX"
LR_REF_PAT <- "^ConnectomeDB.*mouse.*\\.csv$"

LR_W <- 3.0          # inches -> 76 mm
LR_H <- 2.0          # inches -> 51 mm
LR_MAX_LABELS <- 10
LR_PT_BG   <- 0.55   # grey background point size
LR_PT_FG   <- 0.65   # highlighted point size; set to LR_PT_BG to match exactly
LR_LABEL_QUADRANT <- "topright"   # "topright", "bottomleft" or "none"

LR_EVIDENCE <- NULL
LR_MATRISOME_LIGAND_ONLY <- FALSE
LR_SHOW_DISCORDANT <- TRUE

LR_COLS <- c("Both up in Aged"  = "#B57BEE",
             "Both up in Young" = "#007A7A",
             "Discordant"       = "#E08214")

leg_inside <- function(x, y, just = c(x, y)) {
  if (utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "3.5.0")
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "inside",
                   legend.position.inside = c(x, y),
                   legend.justification = just)
  else
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = c(x, y),
                   legend.justification = just)
}

dir.create(LR_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# ---- the database -----------------------------------------------------------
rf <- list.files(LR_REF_DIR, pattern = LR_REF_PAT, full.names = TRUE)
if (!length(rf)) stop("No file matching ", LR_REF_PAT, " in ", LR_REF_DIR)
cdb <- read.csv(rf[1], stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
message("ConnectomeDB rows: ", nrow(cdb), "  (", basename(rf[1]), ")")

if (!"LR Pair" %in% names(cdb))
  stop("No 'LR Pair' column. Columns: ", paste(names(cdb), collapse = ", "))

sp <- strsplit(trimws(cdb[["LR Pair"]]), "[[:space:]]+")
ok <- lengths(sp) == 2
if (any(!ok))
  message("  [WARN] ", sum(!ok),
          " row(s) whose 'LR Pair' is not two symbols, dropped")

pairs <- data.frame(
  ligand   = vapply(sp[ok], `[`, character(1), 1),
  receptor = vapply(sp[ok], `[`, character(1), 2),
  evidence = if ("Evidence" %in% names(cdb)) cdb[["Evidence"]][ok]
             else NA_character_,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

if (!is.null(LR_EVIDENCE)) {
  n0 <- nrow(pairs)
  pairs <- pairs[pairs$evidence %in% LR_EVIDENCE, , drop = FALSE]
  message("  evidence filter '", paste(LR_EVIDENCE, collapse = "/"), "': ",
          nrow(pairs), " of ", n0)
}
n0 <- nrow(pairs)
pairs <- pairs[!duplicated(pairs[, c("ligand", "receptor")]), , drop = FALSE]
message("  unique pairs: ", nrow(pairs), " (", n0 - nrow(pairs),
        " duplicates dropped)")

# ---- the DEG table ----------------------------------------------------------
f <- list.files(OUTPUT_DIR,
                pattern = paste0("^DEG_", LR_TEST, "_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$"),
                recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
if (!length(f)) stop("No DEG file for ", LR_TEST)
d <- read.csv(f[1], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d$lfc <- d[[DEG_LFC_COL]]
d <- d[!is.na(d$padj) & !is.na(d$lfc), c("gene", "lfc", "padj", "pvalue")]
message("Genes tested in ", LR_TEST, ": ", nrow(d))

pairs <- merge(pairs, setNames(d, c("ligand", "lfc_lig", "padj_lig", "p_lig")),
               by = "ligand")
pairs <- merge(pairs, setNames(d, c("receptor", "lfc_rec", "padj_rec", "p_rec")),
               by = "receptor")
message("Pairs with BOTH sides tested: ", nrow(pairs),
        "  (", length(unique(pairs$ligand)), " ligands, ",
        length(unique(pairs$receptor)), " receptors)")
if (!nrow(pairs)) stop("No pair had both sides tested.")

if (exists("matri")) {
  message("  of these, ligand is a matrisome gene: ",
          sum(pairs$ligand %in% matri$gene))
  if (LR_MATRISOME_LIGAND_ONLY) {
    pairs <- pairs[pairs$ligand %in% matri$gene, , drop = FALSE]
    message("  restricted to matrisome ligands: ", nrow(pairs), " pairs")
    if (!nrow(pairs)) stop("No matrisome-ligand pair had both sides tested.")
  }
} else if (LR_MATRISOME_LIGAND_ONLY) {
  stop("LR_MATRISOME_LIGAND_ONLY is TRUE but 'matri' is not in the session. ",
       "Run the {r matrisome-category-bar} chunk above first.")
}

# ---- concordance ------------------------------------------------------------
is_sig <- function(l, p) !is.na(p) & p < PADJ_CUTOFF & abs(l) >= LFC_THRESHOLD
pairs$sig_lig <- is_sig(pairs$lfc_lig, pairs$padj_lig)
pairs$sig_rec <- is_sig(pairs$lfc_rec, pairs$padj_rec)
pairs$both    <- pairs$sig_lig & pairs$sig_rec
pairs$class <- dplyr::case_when(
  pairs$both & pairs$lfc_lig > 0 & pairs$lfc_rec > 0 ~ "Both up in Aged",
  pairs$both & pairs$lfc_lig < 0 & pairs$lfc_rec < 0 ~ "Both up in Young",
  pairs$both                                         ~ "Discordant",
  TRUE                                               ~ "Not both significant")
pairs$pair_label <- paste0(pairs$ligand, "\u2013", pairs$receptor)

message("Ligand significant only  : ", sum(pairs$sig_lig & !pairs$sig_rec))
message("Receptor significant only: ", sum(pairs$sig_rec & !pairs$sig_lig))
print(table(pairs$class))

write.csv(pairs[order(-pairs$both, pairs$class, pairs$ligand, pairs$receptor), ],
          file.path(LR_DIR,
                    paste0("LR_pairs_ConnectomeDB2025_", LR_TEST, ".csv")),
          row.names = FALSE)

# ---- the scatter ------------------------------------------------------------
hi_classes <- c("Both up in Aged", "Both up in Young")
if (LR_SHOW_DISCORDANT) hi_classes <- c(hi_classes, "Discordant")

bg <- pairs[!pairs$class %in% hi_classes, , drop = FALSE]
fg <- pairs[ pairs$class %in% hi_classes, , drop = FALSE]
message("Highlighted: ", nrow(fg), "   background: ", nrow(bg))

lb <- if (nrow(fg)) {
  o <- order(-(abs(fg$lfc_lig) + abs(fg$lfc_rec)))
  fg[o[seq_len(min(LR_MAX_LABELS, nrow(fg)))], , drop = FALSE]
} else fg
if (nrow(fg) > nrow(lb))
  message("  labelling the ", nrow(lb), " largest of ", nrow(fg),
          "; the rest are in the CSV")

ax_abs <- max(abs(c(pairs$lfc_lig, pairs$lfc_rec)), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.08

p <- ggplot(mapping = aes(x = lfc_lig, y = lfc_rec)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-LFC_THRESHOLD, LFC_THRESHOLD),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey78", linewidth = 0.18) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-LFC_THRESHOLD, LFC_THRESHOLD),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey78", linewidth = 0.18) +
  geom_point(data = bg, colour = "grey80", size = LR_PT_BG, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = fg, aes(fill = class), shape = 21, size = LR_PT_FG,
             stroke = 0.16, colour = "black")

if (nrow(lb)) {
  rep_args <- list(
    data = lb, mapping = aes(label = pair_label),
    size = 1.8, seed = 42, max.overlaps = Inf,
    box.padding = 0.16, point.padding = 0.10,
    min.segment.length = 0, segment.size = 0.15,
    segment.colour = "grey55", segment.alpha = 0.8,
    force = 3, max.iter = 20000)
  if (LR_LABEL_QUADRANT == "topright") {
    rep_args$xlim <- c(0, NA); rep_args$ylim <- c(0, NA)
    out <- sum(lb$lfc_lig < 0 | lb$lfc_rec < 0)
  } else if (LR_LABEL_QUADRANT == "bottomleft") {
    rep_args$xlim <- c(NA, 0); rep_args$ylim <- c(NA, 0)
    out <- sum(lb$lfc_lig > 0 | lb$lfc_rec > 0)
  } else out <- 0
  if (out)
    message("  [WARN] ", out, " labelled pair(s) lie outside the ",
            LR_LABEL_QUADRANT, " quadrant, so their labels will be pulled ",
            "across the panel. Set LR_LABEL_QUADRANT <- \"none\" if that ",
            "looks wrong.")
  rep_args$box.padding <- 0.24
  p <- p + do.call(ggrepel::geom_text_repel, rep_args)
}

p <- p +
  scale_fill_manual(values = LR_COLS, name = NULL, drop = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-ax_abs, ax_abs), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-ax_abs, ax_abs), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  labs(x = "L2FC of Ligand", y = "L2FC of Receptor") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 1.6))) +

  theme(axis.text         = element_text(size = 6),
        axis.title        = element_text(size = 6.5),
        axis.ticks        = element_line(linewidth = 0.2),
        legend.direction  = "vertical",
        legend.text       = element_text(size = 5.5),
        legend.key.size   = grid::unit(0.2, "cm"),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.75),
                                         colour = NA),
        legend.margin     = margin(1, 2, 1, 2),
        plot.margin       = margin(3, 4, 3, 3)) +
  leg_inside(0.99, 0.02, just = c(1, 0))

save_plot(p, file.path(LR_DIR,

# Appendix A. Replot and re-threshold from saved CSVs


#No DESeq2, no fgsea. This is the whole workflow for changing `LFC_THRESHOLD`
#(1 to 0.5, say), `PADJ_CUTOFF` or figure geometry: edit the config chunk,
#re-run it, run this. It redraws every volcano and dotplot and rewrites the
#three summary tables with the new cut applied.

#It works because the per-gene statistics do not depend on the threshold. GSEA
#is likewise untouched: it ranks the complete gene list by the Wald statistic,
#so every NES and every GSEA padj is identical before and after.


#```{r replot-from-csv, eval=FALSE}
assert_config_current()

replot_dir <- OUTPUT_DIR   # or point at a single subdir

deg_files <- list.files(replot_dir, pattern = "^DEG_.*_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$",
                        recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
gsea_files <- list.files(replot_dir, pattern = "^GSEA_.*_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$",
                         recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
message("Found ", length(deg_files), " DEG CSVs and ",
        length(gsea_files), " GSEA CSVs")

for (f in deg_files) {
  d <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  lbl <- sub("^DEG_(.*)_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$", "\\1", basename(f))

  # v1/v2 files carry a padj from the composite-null threshold test, or a
  # padj_lfcthr column. Either way they cannot be replotted correctly.
  if (!"log2FoldChange_mle" %in% names(d) || "padj_lfcthr" %in% names(d)) {
    message("[STALE, SKIPPED] ", basename(f),
            " predates CONFIG_VERSION 2026-08-05_v3. Its padj is not the ",
            "plain Wald padj. Re-run the DEG chunk.")
    next
  }
  if (!all(c("gene", "padj", DEG_LFC_COL) %in% names(d))) {
    message("[SKIP] ", basename(f), " missing required columns")
    next
  }
  message(basename(f))
  plot_volcano(d,
    title    = paste0(lbl, ": Aged vs Young (DESeq2 pseudobulk)"),
    out_base = file.path(dirname(f), paste0("Volcano_", lbl, "_Aged_vs_Young")))
}

for (f in gsea_files) {
  g <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  lbl <- sub("^GSEA_(.*)_Aged_vs_Young\\.csv$", "\\1", basename(f))
  if (!all(c("pathway", "NES", "padj", "size") %in% names(g))) {
    message("[SKIP] ", basename(f), " missing required columns")
    next
  }
  message(basename(f))
  plot_gsea_dot(g,
    title    = paste0(lbl, ": GSEA Aged vs Young"),
    out_base = file.path(dirname(f),
                         paste0("GSEA_dotplot_", lbl, "_Aged_vs_Young")))
}

# Re-apply the thresholds to the saved per-gene statistics and rewrite
# DEG_summary_all_tests.csv, GSEA_summary_all_tests.csv and
# GSEA_shared_pathways_across_tests.csv.
rebuild_summaries_from_csv(replot_dir, OUTPUT_DIR)
message("Replot and re-threshold done.")

## Global DEG heatmap, per animal
#Reads the saved `dds` and plots straight from it.
## Global DEG heatmap, per animal

#Reads the saved `dds` and plots straight from it. Nothing is refitted: `DESeq()`
#already stored the dispersions and coefficients, so `results()` and `lfcShrink()`
#here take seconds, not the minutes a re-run would.

#```{r global-deg-heatmap}
# ============================================================================
# CONFIG
# ============================================================================
HM_RDS   <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "0_global", "dds_Global_AllCompartments.rds")
HM_OUT   <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "0_global", "Heatmap_Global_AllDEGs")
HM_W_MM  <- 90
HM_H_MM  <- 120
 
HM_PADJ   <- PADJ_CUTOFF      # 0.05, same object the volcano uses
HM_LFC    <- LFC_THRESHOLD    # 1
HM_SHRINK <- TRUE             # apeglm, matching the volcano
 
# ---- COLOUR SCALE ----------------------------------------------------------
# Three LIGHT stops, in order: negative, middle, positive. Same palette as the
# volcano, so teal = higher in Young and purple = higher in Aged.
HM_COLS <- c(VOLC_COLS[["Up in Young"]], "white", VOLC_COLS[["Up in Aged"]])
 
# The shade reached at HM_BREAK_DARK and held for everything beyond it.
HM_COLS_DARK <- c("#003D3D", "#5C2E8C")
 
# Anchor values:
#     0                 the middle colour (white)
#     |HM_BREAK_LIGHT|  the light shade
#     |HM_BREAK_DARK|   the dark shade
#     beyond            clamped at the dark shade
# White and the pale shades therefore span only -1 to 1. Set HM_BREAK_LIGHT to
# NULL for a single linear stretch.
HM_BREAK_LIGHT <- 1
HM_BREAK_DARK  <- 3
 
# Colourbar ticks: evenly spaced, roughly this many.
HM_CBAR_N_TICKS <- 6
# "anchors" = the bar spans only the range where colour changes
#             (-HM_BREAK_DARK .. +HM_BREAK_DARK).
# "full"    = the bar spans the whole data range, so the clamped region is a
#             flat block at each end. See the note in the drawing code.
HM_CBAR_RANGE <- "anchors"
 
# ---- WHAT A CELL CONTAINS --------------------------------------------------
# DESeq2 gives ONE log2FoldChange per gene, which is why the volcano has one
# dot per gene. A heatmap needs a number per gene PER COLUMN, so with 8 animal
# columns the 8 values have to come from the normalised counts. All three
# options below are log2 quantities; they differ only in what they are measured
# AGAINST.
#
#   "center" log2(normalised count + 1) minus that gene's mean across ALL 8
#            animals. Neither age group is the reference, so young and aged
#            both carry colour. Default, and the right match for a single
#            dendrogram over all 8.
#   "delta"  the same, minus the mean of the 4 YOUNG animals. Young columns
#            then sit near zero by construction. Averaging the aged columns
#            returns DESeq2's log2FoldChange (the printed check confirms it).
#   "zscore" per-gene z-score. Signed, but the colour then means "SDs from this
#            gene's own mean", not fold change.
HM_CELL <- "center"
 
# FALSE = one dendrogram over all 8 animals, order decided by the clustering.
# TRUE  = young block left, aged block right, clustered within each block.
HM_COL_SPLIT <- FALSE
 
# Left NULL the legend title follows HM_CELL. Set a string to override.
HM_LEGEND_TITLE <- NULL
 
# ============================================================================
# PLOTTING FUNCTIONS (base graphics only, no new packages)
# ============================================================================
# =============================================================================
# make_breakpoint_palette
#
# A colour scale with EXPLICIT anchor values rather than one linear stretch:
#
#     0             mid colour (white)
#     |break_light| the light shade   (default 1)
#     |break_dark|  the dark shade    (default 3)
#     beyond        clamped at the dark shade
#
# The value -> POSITION mapping stays linear; only value -> COLOUR is
# piecewise. That keeps tick placement arithmetic simple and correct.
# =============================================================================
make_breakpoint_palette <- function(n, vlim,
                                    cols_light, cols_dark,
                                    break_light = 1, break_dark = 3) {
  stopifnot(length(cols_light) == 3, length(cols_dark) == 2)
  stopifnot(break_dark > break_light, break_light > 0)
  edges   <- seq(-vlim, vlim, length.out = n + 1)
  centres <- (edges[-1] + edges[-(n + 1)]) / 2
 
  a <- pmin(abs(centres), break_dark)            # clamp past the dark anchor
  f <- ifelse(a <= break_light,
              (a / break_light) * 0.5,           # 0 .. 0.5  mid  -> light
              0.5 + (a - break_light) /
                    (break_dark - break_light) * 0.5)  # 0.5 .. 1 light -> dark
 
  # colorRamp with three stops puts the middle stop exactly at 0.5, which is
  # why f is built on that scale: f = 0.5 lands on the light shade by
  # construction rather than by arithmetic that could drift.
  ramp_neg <- grDevices::colorRamp(c(cols_light[2], cols_light[1], cols_dark[1]))
  ramp_pos <- grDevices::colorRamp(c(cols_light[2], cols_light[3], cols_dark[2]))
 
  m <- matrix(NA_real_, n, 3)
  neg <- centres < 0
  if (any(neg))  m[neg, ]  <- ramp_neg(f[neg])
  if (any(!neg)) m[!neg, ] <- ramp_pos(f[!neg])
  grDevices::rgb(m[, 1], m[, 2], m[, 3], maxColorValue = 255)
}
 
# =============================================================================
# plot_deg_heatmap: genes x animals, base graphics only.
# =============================================================================
plot_deg_heatmap <- function(M, age_group, out_base,
                             col_split = FALSE,
                             w_mm = 90, h_mm = 120,
                             cols = c("#007A7A", "white", "#B57BEE"),
                             cols_dark = c("#003D3D", "#5C2E8C"),
                             break_light = 1, break_dark = 3,
                             legend_title = "log2 vs mean",
                             line_lwd = 0.4,
                             n_colours = 255,
                             vlim = NULL, dpi = 600,
                             row_dend_frac = 0.12, col_dend_frac = 0.08,
                             cbar_frac = 0.20,
                             cbar_n_ticks = 6,
                             cbar_range = "anchors",
                             axis_cex  = 0.50,
                             cbar_cex  = 0.50,
                             cbar_title_cex = NULL,
                             title_cex = 0.50,
                             axis_srt = 0,
                             cbar_top = 0.88, cbar_height = 0.25,
                             cbar_title_lines_max = 4,
                             main = NULL) {
 
  stopifnot(ncol(M) == length(age_group))
  young <- which(age_group == "Young")
  aged  <- which(age_group != "Young")
  if (is.null(cbar_title_cex)) cbar_title_cex <- cbar_cex
 
  keep <- apply(M, 1, function(x) stats::sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 1e-12)
  if (sum(!keep)) message("  dropping ", sum(!keep),
                          " gene(s) with no variance across animals")
  M <- M[keep, , drop = FALSE]
 
  cor_dist <- function(A) stats::as.dist(1 - stats::cor(t(A)))
  hr <- stats::hclust(cor_dist(M), method = "average")
  row_ord <- hr$order
 
  block_ord <- function(idx) {
    if (length(idx) < 2) return(list(ord = idx, hc = NULL))
    hc <- stats::hclust(cor_dist(t(M[, idx, drop = FALSE])), method = "average")
    list(ord = idx[hc$order], hc = hc)
  }
  if (col_split) { by <- block_ord(young); ba <- block_ord(aged)
  } else { by <- block_ord(seq_len(ncol(M))); ba <- list(ord = integer(0), hc = NULL) }
  col_ord <- c(by$ord, ba$ord)
 
  D <- M[row_ord, col_ord, drop = FALSE]
  if (is.null(vlim)) vlim <- max(abs(D), na.rm = TRUE)
  brk <- seq(-vlim, vlim, length.out = n_colours + 1)
 
  use_breaks <- !is.null(break_light) && !is.null(break_dark) &&
                break_dark > break_light && break_light > 0
  if (use_breaks) {
    if (break_dark > vlim)
      message("  [NOTE] break_dark (", break_dark, ") exceeds the data range (",
              sprintf("%.2f", vlim), "); the dark shade is never reached.")
    pal <- make_breakpoint_palette(n_colours, vlim, cols, cols_dark,
                                   break_light, break_dark)
    n_clamped <- sum(abs(D) > break_dark, na.rm = TRUE)
    message("  colour anchors: 0 = mid, |", break_light, "| = light, |",
            break_dark, "| = dark, beyond clamped (",
            n_clamped, " of ", length(D), " cells, ",
            sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n_clamped / length(D)), ")")
  } else {
    pal <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(cols)(n_colours)
  }
 
  wrap_to_width <- function(txt, max_w, cex, max_lines) {
    words <- strsplit(txt, "\\s+")[[1]]
    lines <- character(0); cur <- ""
    for (w in words) {
      cand <- if (nzchar(cur)) paste(cur, w) else w
      if (graphics::strwidth(cand, cex = cex) <= max_w || !nzchar(cur)) {
        cur <- cand
      } else { lines <- c(lines, cur); cur <- w }
    }
    lines <- c(lines, cur)
    if (length(lines) > max_lines)
      return(list(lines = txt, cex = cex * max_w /
                    max(graphics::strwidth(txt, cex = cex), 1e-9)))
    list(lines = lines, cex = cex)
  }
 
  draw <- function() {
    op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE); on.exit(par(op), add = TRUE)
    par(oma = c(0, 0, if (is.null(main)) 0.6 else 2.0, 0))
    split_on <- length(ba$ord) > 0
    lay <- if (split_on) rbind(c(0, 1, 2, 0), c(3, 4, 4, 5)) else
                         rbind(c(0, 1, 0), c(2, 3, 4))
    nc <- ncol(D)
    graphics::layout(lay,
      widths  = if (split_on)
                  c(row_dend_frac * nc, length(by$ord), length(ba$ord),
                    cbar_frac * nc)
                else c(row_dend_frac * nc, length(by$ord), cbar_frac * nc),
      heights = c(col_dend_frac, 1))
 
    hm_mar_b <- 2.0
    dend <- function(hc, horiz = FALSE, n_leaf = NULL) {
      par(mar = if (horiz) c(hm_mar_b, 0, 0, 0) else c(0, 0, 0, 0),
          lwd = line_lwd)
      if (is.null(hc)) { plot.new(); return(invisible()) }
      d <- stats::as.dendrogram(hc)
      if (horiz) plot(rev(d), horiz = TRUE, axes = FALSE, yaxs = "i",
                      leaflab = "none", ylim = c(0.5, n_leaf + 0.5),
                      xlim = c(attr(d, "height"), 0))
      else plot(d, axes = FALSE, xaxs = "i", leaflab = "none")
    }
    dend(by$hc)
    if (length(ba$ord)) dend(ba$hc)
    dend(hr, horiz = TRUE, n_leaf = nrow(D))
 
    par(mar = c(hm_mar_b, 0, 0, 0), lwd = line_lwd)
    graphics::image(x = seq_len(ncol(D)), y = seq_len(nrow(D)),
                    z = t(D), col = pal, breaks = brk,
                    ylim = c(0.5, nrow(D) + 0.5), yaxs = "i",
                    axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", useRaster = TRUE)
    box(lwd = line_lwd)
    usr <- par("usr")
    text(x = seq_len(ncol(D)), y = usr[3] - (usr[4] - usr[3]) * 0.012,
         labels = colnames(D), srt = axis_srt, adj = c(0.5, 1),
         cex = axis_cex, xpd = NA)
 
    # ---- colourbar ---------------------------------------------------
    par(mar = c(0, 0.6, 0, 0.6), lwd = line_lwd)
    plot.new(); plot.window(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1))
    y1 <- cbar_top; y0 <- cbar_top - cbar_height
 
    # WHAT RANGE THE BAR SPANS.
    #   "anchors" (default) the bar runs -break_dark .. +break_dark, i.e. only
    #                       the range where the colour actually changes.
    #   "full"              the bar runs -vlim .. +vlim, so the clamped region
    #                       is drawn as a flat block at each end.
    # This matters once ticks are evenly spaced. With "full" and vlim = 8 the
    # ticks land at 8, 4, 0, -4, -8, and 4 and 8 point at IDENTICAL colour,
    # which tells the reader they can distinguish values that the scale has
    # already merged. "anchors" removes the flat band instead of labelling it.
    bar_hi <- if (use_breaks && cbar_range == "anchors") break_dark else vlim
    bar_pal <- if (use_breaks && cbar_range == "anchors")
                 make_breakpoint_palette(n_colours, bar_hi, cols, cols_dark,
                                         break_light, break_dark)
               else pal
 
    yy <- seq(y0, y1, length.out = n_colours + 1)
    rect(0.05, yy[-length(yy)], 0.45, yy[-1], col = bar_pal, border = NA)
    rect(0.05, y0, 0.45, y1, border = "black", lwd = line_lwd)
 
    # Evenly spaced ticks. pretty() over a symmetric range returns a symmetric,
    # evenly spaced set, so 0 and the anchors still land on ticks whenever the
    # spacing divides them.
    tk  <- pretty(c(-bar_hi, bar_hi), cbar_n_ticks)
    tk  <- tk[abs(tk) <= bar_hi + 1e-9]
    lab <- format(tk)
    if (use_breaks && vlim > break_dark) {
      # The extremes are clamped, so the end labels say so rather than
      # implying the bar stops where the data stop.
      lab[which.max(tk)] <- paste0(">=", format(max(tk)))
      lab[which.min(tk)] <- paste0("<=", format(min(tk)))
    }
    ty <- y0 + (tk + bar_hi) / (2 * bar_hi) * (y1 - y0)
    segments(0.45, ty, 0.52, ty, lwd = line_lwd)
    text(0.56, ty, lab, adj = 0, cex = cbar_cex, xpd = NA)
 
    wr <- wrap_to_width(legend_title, 0.96, cbar_title_cex,
                        cbar_title_lines_max)
    lh <- graphics::strheight("Ag", cex = wr$cex) * 1.25
    for (i in seq_along(wr$lines))
      text(0.02, y1 + 0.02 + lh * (length(wr$lines) - i),
           wr$lines[i], adj = c(0, 0), cex = wr$cex, xpd = NA)
    if (!is.null(main)) mtext(main, outer = TRUE, cex = title_cex, line = 0.2)
  }
 
  w_in <- w_mm / 25.4; h_in <- h_mm / 25.4
  grDevices::png(paste0(out_base, ".png"), width = w_in, height = h_in,
                 units = "in", res = dpi, bg = "white"); draw(); grDevices::dev.off()
  ok <- TRUE
  if (requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE)) {
    svglite::svglite(paste0(out_base, ".svg"), width = w_in, height = h_in)
    draw(); grDevices::dev.off()
  } else {
    ok <- tryCatch({
      grDevices::svg(paste0(out_base, ".svg"), width = w_in, height = h_in,
                     bg = "white"); draw(); grDevices::dev.off(); TRUE
    }, error = function(e) { message("  SVG failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); FALSE })
  }
  message("  wrote ", basename(out_base), ".png",
          if (ok) paste0(" + ", basename(out_base), ".svg") else "",
          "  (", nrow(D), " genes x ", ncol(D), " animals, ",
          w_mm, " x ", h_mm, " mm)")
  invisible(list(matrix = D, row_hclust = hr, vlim = vlim, palette = pal))
}
 
# ============================================================================
# 1. READ THE STORED FIT
# DESeq2 is already attached by the setup chunk, so these are called plainly;
# SummarizedExperiment (which provides colData) comes with it.
# ============================================================================
stopifnot(file.exists(HM_RDS))
dds <- readRDS(HM_RDS)
message("dds: ", nrow(dds), " genes x ", ncol(dds), " pseudobulk samples")
 
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("age_group", "Aged", "Young"), alpha = HM_PADJ)
if (HM_SHRINK) {
  # Same two lines the DEG chunk uses, so the log2FC here is the log2FC there.
  coef_name <- resultsNames(dds)[grepl("age_group", resultsNames(dds))]
  res <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = coef_name, type = "apeglm", quiet = TRUE)
}
rdf <- as.data.frame(res)
rdf$gene <- rownames(rdf)
 
deg <- rdf$gene[!is.na(rdf$padj) & rdf$padj < HM_PADJ &
                  abs(rdf$log2FoldChange) > HM_LFC]
message("DEGs at padj < ", HM_PADJ, " and |log2FC| > ", HM_LFC, ": ",
        length(deg), "  (", sum(rdf$log2FoldChange[match(deg, rdf$gene)] > 0),
        " up / ", sum(rdf$log2FoldChange[match(deg, rdf$gene)] < 0), " down)")
stopifnot(length(deg) >= 2)
 
# ============================================================================
# 2. PER-ANIMAL VALUES
# ============================================================================
# counts(normalized = TRUE) applies the median-of-ratios size factors that
# DESeq2 already estimated, so the heatmap and the DEG call share one
# normalisation and cannot drift apart.
nc  <- counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)[deg, , drop = FALSE]
lg  <- log2(nc + 1)
cd  <- as.data.frame(colData(dds))
age <- as.character(cd$age_group)
colnames(lg) <- if (!is.null(cd$animal_id)) as.character(cd$animal_id) else
  sub("__.*", "", colnames(lg))
 
if (HM_CELL == "zscore") {
  M <- t(scale(t(lg)))
  ttl <- "z-score"
} else if (HM_CELL == "delta") {
  young_cols <- which(age == "Young")
  stopifnot(length(young_cols) >= 2)
  M <- lg - rowMeans(lg[, young_cols, drop = FALSE])
  ttl <- "log2 vs young"
} else {
  M <- lg - rowMeans(lg)
  ttl <- "log2 vs mean"
}
if (!is.null(HM_LEGEND_TITLE)) ttl <- HM_LEGEND_TITLE
 
# Sanity check, reported rather than assumed: rebuilding the contrast from the
# per-animal columns should reproduce DESeq2's own estimate. If it does not,
# the figure and the statistics are describing different things.
if (HM_CELL %in% c("delta", "center")) {
  # Subtracting a per-gene constant cancels in a group difference, so this
  # check is identical for "delta" and "center".
  approx <- rowMeans(M[, age != "Young", drop = FALSE]) -
            rowMeans(M[, age == "Young", drop = FALSE])
  rr <- suppressWarnings(
    stats::cor(approx, rdf$log2FoldChange[match(rownames(M), rdf$gene)],
               use = "complete.obs"))
  message("per-animal construction vs DESeq2 log2FC: Pearson r = ",
          sprintf("%.3f", rr))
  if (!is.na(rr) && rr < 0.8)
    warning("r < 0.8: the columns and the DESeq2 estimate disagree. ",
            "Do not use this figure until that is resolved.")
}
 
# ============================================================================
# 3. DRAW
# ============================================================================
res_hm <- plot_deg_heatmap(
  M, age, HM_OUT, col_split = HM_COL_SPLIT,
  w_mm = HM_W_MM, h_mm = HM_H_MM,
  cols = HM_COLS, cols_dark = HM_COLS_DARK,
  break_light = HM_BREAK_LIGHT, break_dark = HM_BREAK_DARK,
  cbar_n_ticks = HM_CBAR_N_TICKS, cbar_range = HM_CBAR_RANGE,
  legend_title = ttl,
  main = paste0("Global: all DEGs (", nrow(M), " genes)\naged vs young"))
 
write.csv(res_hm$matrix, paste0(HM_OUT, ".csv"))
message("Saved: ", HM_OUT, ".png / .svg / .csv")
```
